commits.pr_title: [Perf][MoE] Add H200 FP8 config for GLM-5.3-Flash TP8
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Adding the missing H200 MoE configuration improved GLM-5.3-Flash TP8 output throughput by **10.9%** and reduced **p90 time per output token by 16%** at concurrency 16. These measurements predate #63820; current-main gains have not been remeasured.

## Claims

Avoids falling back to the generic MoE configuration.

## Validation

`python -m json.tool`, `cmp`, and `pre-commit run` passed. No observed GSM8K regression in the measured H200 setup.

## Details

Reuses the existing E=256 configuration for the E=288,N=256 shape. No overlapping config PR found; #66347 only changes the tuning script.

commits.pr_title: [Transformers backend] Support LoRA on lm_head and on any input embedding name
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Support LoRA adapters that target `lm_head`, or input embeddings not named `embed_tokens`, on the Transformers modeling backend. Part of serving Llama with the backend (#66547). The aux hidden state layer 0 changes moved to #66546.

## Claims

- LoRA adapters targeting `lm_head` load on the Transformers backend; previously they were rejected with `expected target modules in {...} but received ['lm_head', 'lm_head']`.
- The input embedding's name comes from the model's `get_input_embeddings()` instead of being hard-coded to `embed_tokens`, so adapters targeting e.g. GPT-NeoX's `embed_in` or GPT-2's `wte` load.
- `SupportsLoRA.embedding_modules` is no longer a `ClassVar`, matching `packed_modules_mapping`, since the LoRA runner reads it from the model instance.

## Validation

B200. Both new tests fail on `main` (adapter rejected) and pass on this PR. `test_lora_on_input_embeddings_not_named_embed_tokens` applies a random PEFT adapter to Pythia-70m's `embed_in` and checks it changes the output.

```bash
pytest tests/lora/test_llama_tp.py -k "test_llama_lora_transformers_backend or test_llama_lora"
pytest tests/lora/test_transformers_model.py
pytest tests/models/transformers/test_backend.py -k "not distributed"
```

Also passing: native `test_llama_lora`, `test_ilama_lora` and `test_backend.py` (38 passed).

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Kernel] Support persistent_topk on ROCm
commits.pr_body:
- Build `persistent_topk`, its FilteredTopK and sampled_topk tiers, and the shared exact overflow recovery from #62936 with hipcc (wave64-safe `TOPK_*` ballot/shuffle macros, HIP acquire load, clang-compatible `exact_topk_rescan` defaults).
- On gfx950 (at least 144 KiB of LDS), run every batch through `sampled_topk_kernel`, one workgroup per row, and cut clustered rows at the exact sampled rank. gfx942 keeps the persistent kernel. Return early on an empty batch.
- Place the decode logits of `rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` after the top-k workspace, so `persistent_topk`'s row states no longer overwrite them.
- Allow the explicit `persistent` sparse-indexer backend on ROCm; `auto` still resolves to `per_row`.
- Route `cooperative` / `persistent` through `SparseIndexerTopk._row_ends`, so `(B,)` `seq_lens` with `next_n > 1` no longer raise "lengths size mismatch".
- Run the `persistent_topk` tests on ROCm, including #62936's candidate-overflow cases, add a test for the logits overlap, and add `persistent` to `benchmark_top_k_per_row_decode.py`.
- Document `persistent` on ROCm in the `KernelConfig` docstring, and run the persistent top-k tests in the MI355 DeepSeek V4 kernels step (MI300 already runs the file).

On ROCm the sparse indexer could only use the in-tree `per_row` top-k or AITER, and asking for `persistent` failed because the op was compiled out. This PR builds it on top of #62936, which is now merged and makes the persistent and filtered paths exact on candidate overflow, so the ROCm-only rescan forks from earlier revisions are gone and ROCm shares that code. Wiring it into GLM-5.3-Flash showed that its decode logits and the top-k workspace both start at offset 0 of the shared workspace, which corrupts row 0 whenever the multi-CTA path runs (gfx942). CUDA is not affected, because its paged MQA logits are not workspace views, and ROCm on main is not either, because it rejects this backend. The backend stays opt-in, so default ROCm top-k selection does not change, but on gfx942, gfx950 and RDNA the decode logits now sit 1 MiB further into the workspace for every backend. On MI355X with k=2048 it is 2.2-2.6x faster than `per_row` and on par with AITER, and in GLM-5.3-Flash serving on this revision it selects exactly what `per_row` selects, with unchanged GSM8K 25-shot accuracy and throughput. This branch is stacked on #62298 (head b47c6178f1), so until that merges the diff against main includes #62298; this PR's own changes are `a2f04ca777..11871cef49` and `2fe6f7e5df`, plus merges of main and #62298.

<details>
<summary>Tests, end-to-end, benchmarks, open items and duplicate check</summary>

**gfx950 dispatch (MI355X, sampled path).**

```
pytest tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py -k "persistent or sparse_indexer"   # 10x in a loop
206 passed, 50 skipped, 409 deselected                                         # all 10 runs
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py
1 failed, 403 passed, 261 skipped    # test_aiter_decode_topk_matches_per_row_under_mtp compares AITER
                                     # with per_row; neither path changes in this PR
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py \
  test_rocm_glm5next_sparse.py test_rocm_paged_mqa_context_lens.py \
  test_rocm_aiter_triton_sparse_mla.py test_sparse_mla_backends.py
171 passed, 269 skipped
```

After merging main (b4a0830f66) and #62298's head (85e0eae614), the persistent group gave the same 206 passed, 50 skipped in all 10 runs, the AITER group the same 1 failed, 403 passed, and the sparse-attention group 177 passed, 271 skipped (main added tests), with one failure in `test_sparse_backend_decode_correctness[...-large_q_pure_prefill-ROCMAiterMLA]`. That test feeds synthetic top-k indices to the attention backend, never reaches this PR's code, and failed 1 of 10 times when looped alone.

The skips in the persistent group are CUDA-only, cooperative, FlashInfer and DeepSelect cases. A randomized `SparseIndexerTopk("persistent")` stress run compared values against `torch.topk`: 2,000 cases, 0 failures (k ∈ {512, 1024, 2048}, 0-64 requests, `next_n` 1-4, 1-D and 2-D `seq_lens`, empty batches, NaN/inf, ties, clustered rows). The ROCm-only clustered-rows test from the previous revision (16K, 32K and 128K rows of `randn * 0.01 + 3`, every case failed before) passes on #62936's shared paths, so it was dropped in favour of #62936's overflow test. Because gfx950 always dispatches to `sampled_topk`, some re-enabled tests (for example `test_persistent_topk_reused_group_after_short_row` and `test_persistent_topk_sampled_graph`) pass there without reaching the persistent kernel; the multi-CTA paths get real coverage on MI300 CI and in the gfx942-dispatch runs below. Validation covers gfx950 (MI355X) and gfx942 (MI300X); RDNA (wave32) compiles and admits the backend but was not tested.

**gfx942 dispatch (persistent kernel).** On MI300X (`sharedMemPerBlockOptin` is 64 KiB, so the persistent kernel runs instead of `sampled_topk`), the persistent group gave 176 passed, 80 skipped in 10 of 10 runs; the skips are the sampled-top-k tests that need 144 KiB of LDS and the CUDA-only backends. Before MI300X was available, a local build that capped `max_smem_per_block` and occupancy at 64 KiB on MI355X gave the same counts, and the stress run on it gave 2,000 cases with 0 failures. The cap was never committed.

**Logits overlap.** `rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` returned its logits at workspace offset 0, the same place `SparseIndexerTopk` takes the `persistent_topk` workspace from. On the multi-CTA path the op clears its per-group row states there (`cudaMemsetAsync` in `topk.cu`) and then keeps barrier counters and histograms in them. In GLM-5.3-Flash serving with gfx942 dispatch this made 17,346 of 18,964 calls return wrong rows, all in row 0. The logits now come from the same `get_simultaneous` call as a top-k slot in front of them, and the profiling reservation uses the same layout. `test_persistent_topk_on_rocm_paged_mqa_logits` changed 3,088 logits (four groups' row states) with gfx942 dispatch before the fix and none after. On MI300X the test fails the same way with the logits moved back to offset 0 and passes with the fix:

```
pytest tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py -k test_persistent_topk_on_rocm_paged_mqa_logits   # MI300X
1 failed: Tensor-likes are not equal! Mismatched elements: 3088 / 327680 (0.9%)   # logits at offset 0
1 passed                                                                          # this PR
```

Native gfx950 never runs that path, so there it passes either way; ROCm CI runs `test_top_k_per_row.py` on MI300, and the persistent group on MI355.

**End to end, GLM-5.3-Flash (amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4, TP2, MI355X, AITER on, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` graphs, k=512 under kpool 4), on this revision (11871cef49) against its base (1966abc5b2).** For this model, prompts of at most 2,048 tokens never reach the top-k: both decode (`_fill_short_decode_causal_indices`) and prefill (`short_prefill`) fill every causal index and skip it. GSM8K 5-shot (at most 1,521 tokens) and a 1K/1K bench therefore cannot tell the backends apart, so accuracy is compared on GSM8K 25-shot (3,289-5,091 tokens; every request runs the top-k).
- Exactness: an in-model hook re-ran `per_row` on a pre-call copy of the logits for every `persistent` call and compared the selected values per row. It found 0 mismatching rows in 6.94M decode rows per TP rank (2.51M without MTP, 4.43M with MTP 3-token speculation; GSM8K 25-shot plus 1K/8K/32K serving). Fewer than 0.01% of rows pick a different index among tied values.
- The same check with gfx942 dispatch (the 64 KiB LDS cap described above) found 0 mismatching rows in another 4.48M decode rows per rank, including 140K-token prompts with MTP that take the radix path. A capped server with graphs completed 1K/8K/32K serving and 8 of 8 140K-token requests with no fault.
- GSM8K 25-shot (flexible-extract), default vs `persistent`: 0.9295/0.9287 vs 0.9295/0.9265 over two runs each.
- Default backend, this PR vs base, serving throughput (tok/s) and mean TPOT (ms): 1K/1K at c=32 1837.0 vs 1843.6 and 16.53 vs 16.52; 8K/1K at c=16 844.3 vs 844.5 and 16.12 vs 16.01; 32K/1K at c=8 385.8 vs 387.0 and 15.34 vs 15.20. The new logits offset did not trip the locked workspace.
- `persistent` vs default on this PR: 8K/1K 851.3 vs 844.3 tok/s (TPOT 15.80 vs 16.12 ms) and 32K/1K 386.9 vs 385.8 tok/s (15.13 vs 15.34 ms). With MTP (both servers measured side by side on other GPUs): 865.3 vs 863.2 and 405.8 vs 414.0 tok/s.
- MI300X (gfx942, native persistent kernel), same model at TP2 on e707c976bd: the same check found 0 mismatching rows in 2.51M decode rows per rank and in 2.76M with MTP, including 140K-token prompts on the radix path. GSM8K 25-shot, `per_row` vs `persistent`: 0.9196/0.9257 vs 0.9196/0.9166. With graphs, `persistent` completed 8K/32K serving and 8 of 8 140K-token requests with no fault, at 73.5 vs 72.3 tok/s (8K/1K) and 36.6 vs 36.1 tok/s (32K/1K) against `per_row`. Decode takes about 210 ms per token for both backends on this node, so these throughput numbers say little about the top-k itself.
- On the previous revision, the radix path with gfx942 dispatch and 135K-190K-token prompts showed 0 wrong rows in 5.28M checked radix rows with #63475, and 37 of 37 benchmark runs completed. Without #63475 there were 107-137 wrong rows per 2.6M, and every server died with a GPU memory access fault within minutes. Those runs gave `persistent_topk` a private copy of the logits to keep the overlap above out of the measurement.

**Intermittent corruption seen on 2026-10-24.** In an earlier round, 8 of 144 test runs failed with buffers corrupted that the op never writes. It did not reproduce in more than 400 later runs, including every run above. The dumps showed corruption in buffers written before the op ran while the op was exact on what it read, so it is attributed to the environment during a busy window on the shared node, and it is being retested on ROCm 10.

**Benchmark.** CUDA-graph timing on the shapes `benchmark_top_k_per_row_decode.py` uses, us per call, k=2048, width 163840, all outputs checked exact, AITER 0.1.26. `benchmark_top_k_per_row_decode.py --backends native aiter persistent --graph` times the same kernels.

| logits | rows | width | per_row | aiter | persistent |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| randn | 1 | 4K | 18.5 | 8.2 | 5.5 |
| randn | 64 | 16K | 26.3 | 13.0 | 16.1 |
| randn | 256 | 32K | 40.1 | 19.0 | 27.3 |
| randn | 64 | 128K | 93.4 | 43.7 | 35.5 |
| randn | 256 | 128K | 102.0 | 50.3 | 41.1 |
| clustered | 1 | 4K | 26.4 | 10.5 | 12.4 |
| clustered | 64 | 16K | 56.5 | 21.5 | 27.1 |
| clustered | 1 | 32K | 90.0 | 40.9 | 44.3 |
| clustered | 64 | 128K | 311.5 | 133.9 | 60.1 |
| clustered | 256 | 128K | 329.9 | 143.8 | 65.7 |

Over all 36 shapes per distribution (1/4/16/64/128/256 rows x 4K-128K), persistent is 2.23x faster than `per_row` and 1.08x faster than AITER on randn logits (ahead on 22/36), and 2.63x faster than `per_row` and 0.98x against AITER on clustered logits (`randn * 0.01 + 3`, ahead on 9/36). Against the previous revision with the ROCm-only forks, #62936's shared paths are 5.7% slower on randn (mostly 32K rows) and 10% faster on clustered logits.

**Duplicate check.** Searched open PRs for `persistent_topk ROCm`, `persistent topk hip`, `ROCm sparse indexer topk`, `rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits workspace`, `topk workspace alias`, `_row_ends`, `lengths size mismatch` and `sampled_topk`:
- #50470 routes sparse-indexer decode top-k through AITER, a different backend that complements this one.
- #55122 changes how `persistent_topk` selects ties on CUDA and does not build it for ROCm.
- #38704 moves ROCm sparse-indexer allocations into the workspace manager and does not touch the top-k workspace.
- #41748 replaces the `cudaMemsetAsync` of the row states in `topk.cu` with in-kernel cleanup. It does not build for ROCm or move the logits, but it touches the same code and will need a rebase against whichever lands second.

No open PR builds `persistent_topk` for ROCm, fixes the logits overlap or fixes the `_row_ends` routing.

</details>

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

commits.pr_title: [CI][Test] Bias test_stop_reason toward the stop token
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose
`test_stop_reason` samples (temperature 1, seed 42) for up to 1024 tokens with distilgpt2 and requires every prompt to stop at ".". The sampled tokens depend on batch composition (bf16), and the batch changes with timing because stop-string matches abort requests mid-batch, so some runs take a trajectory that never emits "." and finishes with "length". This flakes on `:amd: (MI355 DPX) Async Engine, Inputs, Utils, Worker` since #57599 moved the step to mi355_dpx on 2026-09-25 (about 3.6% of attempts, almost all in the stop-string block). It is not a seeded-sampling bug: batch size 1 or `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` make it reproducible.

Keep the strict per-prompt checks and add `logit_bias={stop_token_id: 5.0}` to the stop-token and stop-string requests, so every trajectory emits "." early.

## Test Plan
MI300X, CI image for main@38955340b7, original test vs. biased test.

## Test Result
- Original: fails on 2/12 seeds (outputs run to 1002 and 1005 tokens without ".").
- Biased: 24/24 passed over 12 seeds on two GPUs, plus 30/30 fresh runs with seed 42; longest output 160 tokens.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Close the parent's listening sockets after launching the Rust frontend
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Part of #65155. The parent process kept its copies of the HTTP and gRPC sockets after passing them to the Rust frontend, so both ports kept listening after Rust closed its listeners at shutdown. Clients that connected during a drain were never answered. This closes them right after `Popen`, where the ZMQ listeners are already closed.

## Claims

- During a drain, new HTTP and gRPC clients are refused instead of hanging. Requests already running still finish.
- New gRPC clients can still hang while another gRPC call is open. That's the Rust side of the issue and needs a separate fix.

## Validation

Ran `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 vllm serve HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct --grpc-port 50052 --shutdown-timeout 40` on the `vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:latest` image (0.33.0, same `RustFrontendProcessManager` as main; "After" has this change applied). I kept a long HTTP completion running, sent SIGTERM, and connected to each port 2s later:

| | New HTTP client | New gRPC client | In-flight request |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before | no reply after 5s | `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` after 5s | 200 |
| After | connection refused | `UNAVAILABLE` (connection refused) | 200 |

The new test gives the manager real listening sockets and a fake `Popen`, then checks that connecting afterwards is refused. It fails on main with `DID NOT RAISE ConnectionRefusedError`.

```
pytest tests/entrypoints/launchers/api_server/test_api_server_process_manager.py  # 13 passed
```

## Details

The child already has the fds through `pass_fds` once `Popen` returns, and the parent doesn't touch the sockets after that. `test_rust_frontend_inherits_grpc_listener` now reads the fds before the manager closes them.

#64426 adds per-rank sockets to this class, so whichever PR lands second should close those too.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][MoRIIO] Support PP for prefill instance in PD disaggregated serving with MoRI WRITE mode
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

In WRITE mode, `MoRIIOConnector` assumes one prefill rank per TP index that writes every layer. With pipeline parallelism, the index is shared for the stages, so the stages collide on ports and the later ones fail to start. Each stage also numbers its layers from zero, so a stage that does write puts them on the decode instance's first layers. This PR lets a prefill instance under MoRIIO's WRITE mode use pipeline parallelism, with each stage writing the layers it holds to the decode addresses of those same layers and a decode rank finishing the transfer only after every stage has reported.



## Claims

- A prefill instance can now run with pipeline parallelism in WRITE mode. Each stage writes its own layers, and decoding starts only after every stage has reported.
- For MLA models the main gain is prefill capacity. On GLM-5.2 and GLM-5.3 (8 × MI355X), a TP1 × PP4 prefill instance holds about 4× the KV cache of a TP4 one (4.12× and 4.02×) and serves 41.9 % and 27.1 % more tokens per GPU on 32K-token prompts at 16 concurrent requests, with TTFT p50 down 42 % and 30 %.
- The peer's layer addresses are now looked up by layer name. This also fixes a case without pipeline parallelism where a decode instance with an MTP layer is fed by a prefill instance without MTP.
- Combinations the connector don't support fail at startup with an error that articulates the setting.



## Validation

### Unit tests

The new tests added are CPU tests in `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_pipeline_parallel.py` (21 cases, `cpu_test`), ROCm + MoRI cases in `test_moriio_connector.py` (per-stage ports and MoRI engine keys, refused PP roles and layouts), and one case in `test_moriio_hma_scheduler.py` (the handshake advertises each layer's region). Reverting each part of the change to main's behaviour makes its tests fail.

| Behaviours | Tests | Main | With this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Peer layer address by local position | `test_peer_with_an_extra_draft_layer_is_addressed_by_name`, `test_stage_writes_each_layer_at_the_peer_address_of_that_layer` | 2 failed | 2 passed |
| Port offset without the stage term | `test_every_stage_worker_binds_its_own_ports` | 3 failed, 1 passed (no PP) | 4 passed |
| First stage does not forward the decode's messages | test_every_stage_gets_the_allocation_and_release | 3 failed | 3 passed |
| Decode counts `write_done` messages, not senders | `test_decode_rank_waits_for_every_distinct_stage` | 1 failed | 1 passed |
| Producer `num_writers` without the stage count | `test_stage_reports_every_stage_as_a_writer_and_names_itself` | 1 failed | 1 passed |
| Consumer does not mark a settled transfer | `test_first_stage_failure_fails_the_transfer_once` | 1 failed | 1 passed |

### End-to-end verification with GLM-5.2/GLM-5.3

These runs use a single node of 8 MI355X GPUs, with the prefill instance on GPUs 0-3 and a TP4 decode instance on GPUs 4-7, MoRIIO WRITE over xGMI and the toy proxy from vLLM example. Both instances use block size 64, fp8 KV and index caches, MTP with 3 speculative tokens, prefix caching, chunked prefill at 32,768 tokens, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` graphs, the glm47 parsers and thinking on, with `--max-num-seqs 256`. The TP1 × PP4 prefill instances use `VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=22,20,20,16`. Note that the runs below includes #64330, which fixes the completion-wait hang over xGMI.

| Model | Prefill instance | Prefill KV cache (tokens) | Delta (%) | GSM8K 20-shot, flexible-extract / strict-match | Total tok/s per GPU, 32K in / 256 out, 16 concurrent | Delta (%) | TTFT p50 (s) | Delta (%) | TTFT p99 (s) | Delta (%) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GLM-5.2 | TP4 | 2,622,592 | | 0.9340 / 0.9348 |3,220 | | 16.01 | | 19.86 | |
| GLM-5.2 | TP1 × PP4 | 10,817,536 | +312 | 0.9325 / 0.9333 |4,568 | +41.9 | 9.35 | −41.6 | 19.76 | −0.5 |
| GLM-5.3 | TP4 | 2,753,664 | | 0.9689 / 0.9689 | 2,977 | | 17.64 | | 21.44 | |
| GLM-5.3 | TP1 × PP4 | 11,079,424 | +302 | 0.9674 / 0.9682 | 3,783 | +27.1 | 12.30 | −30.3 | 23.30 | +8.7 |

Throughput is per GPU over all eight GPUs, on 128 prompts, and every request completed without a preemption. GSM8K is 20-shot with the chat template, few-shot as multi-turn, 16K max tokens and 32 concurrent requests, with a standard error of ±0.007 (GLM-5.2) and ±0.005 (GLM-5.3) per run. No completion wait failed or timed out during the runs, and no transfer error was logged.

<details>
<summary>GLM commands</summary>

```bash
# environment, both instances (GLM-5.3 adds VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP8BMM=0 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4BMM=0)
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 \
  VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4
# for GLM-5.3, serve amd/GLM-5.3-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8 --revision bcd1ec31dc1fd474b9997dd2476c92687790b83d --quantization quark
COMMON="--block-size 64 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention-config {\"indexer_kv_dtype\":\"fp8\"} --moe-backend aiter \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --enable-chunked-prefill --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 --enable-prefix-caching \
  --max-num-seqs 256 --compilation-config {\"cudagraph_mode\":\"FULL_DECODE_ONLY\"} \
  --speculative-config {\"method\":\"mtp\",\"num_speculative_tokens\":3} \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser glm47"

# proxy
python3 examples/disaggregated/disaggregated_serving/moriio_toy_proxy_server.py --port 8000 --service-discovery-port 8003

# prefill, TP4
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 MORI_IO_XGMI_SCATTER_GATHER_THRESHOLD=0 \
vllm serve amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 --served-model-name GLM-5.2 --port 8001 --tensor-parallel-size 4 $COMMON \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MoRIIOConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_connector_extra_config":{"backend":"xgmi","read_mode":"false","proxy_ip":"127.0.0.1","proxy_ping_port":"8003","http_port":"8001","handshake_port":"8010","notify_port":"8018"}}'
# prefill, TP1 x PP4, is the same with
#   VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=22,20,20,16 ... --tensor-parallel-size 1 --pipeline-parallel-size 4

# decode, TP4
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4,5,6,7 \
vllm serve amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 --served-model-name GLM-5.2 --port 8002 --tensor-parallel-size 4 $COMMON \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MoRIIOConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer","kv_connector_extra_config":{"backend":"xgmi","read_mode":"false","proxy_ip":"127.0.0.1","proxy_ping_port":"8003","http_port":"8002","handshake_port":"8026","notify_port":"8034"}}'

# accuracy
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args "model=GLM-5.2,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=32,max_gen_toks=16384,max_retries=3,timeout=3600" \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 20 --batch_size 1 --apply_chat_template --fewshot_as_multiturn

# benchmark
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --endpoint /v1/completions --model GLM-5.2 \
  --tokenizer amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 --dataset-name random --random-input-len 32768 --random-output-len 256 \
  --random-range-ratio 0 --ignore-eos --num-prompts 128 --max-concurrency 16 --request-rate inf --seed 1029 \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,90,99
```

</details>



## Details

For MLA models, a TP*n* prefill instance keeps a full copy of each layer's latent KV on every TP rank. Splitting the layers across pipeline stages instead lets the same GPUs hold up to *n* times the tokens, which is what makes a TP1 × PP4 prefill instance attractive for models like GLM-5.2 and GLM-5.3.

With this PR, a WRITE transfer from a pipeline-parallel prefill instance goes through four steps.
1. The decode scheduler sends the block allocation (and, on a full prefix hit or an abort, the release) to the notify ports of the first stage, as for a pipeline-free prefill instance.
2. Each worker of the first stage forwards every message from the decode to the same worker of the later stages on its node.
3. Each stage writes the layers it holds into those blocks, at the decode addresses of the same layers.
4. Each stage sends `write_done`, and a decode rank finishes the transfer after the last one.

On main none of this holds. Every stage binds the same handshake and notify ports and registers the same MoRI engine key, so stage 1 fails to start. The decode side only notifies `range(prefill_tp)` ports, so with TP1 only stage 0 ever learns the decode blocks. And the peer's layer address comes from this worker's own registration order.

```
vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/moriio/moriio_connector.py's MoRIIOConnectorWorker._remote_layer_mr_offset
idx = self.layer_base_addr_index[layer_name]
...
return remote_moriio_meta.kv_caches_base_addr[idx] - mr_base
```

So stage `s` writes its first layer at the decode's layer 0. On top of that, a decode rank finishes after `num_writers` messages, and `num_writers` comes from the TP mapping alone (1 for prefill TP1 → decode TP4), so it would start decoding after the first stage.

The layer lookup is also wrong without pipeline parallelism whenever the two instances register different layers. vLLM's KV planner groups layers by spec and puts a draft layer in its target's group, so for DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.2 and GLM-5.3 the decode's MTP latent cache sits after the target latents and before every indexer cache. A prefill instance without MTP then silently writes indexer cache 0 into the decode's MTP region, and indexer cache `j` into region `j - 1`.

This PR makes the following changes.
- It adds a stage term to the port offset, `pp_rank * tp_size * dp_size_local`, so stage 0 keeps the ports of a pipeline-free instance, and it appends `:pp<rank>` to the MoRI engine key when PP > 1.
- It has each worker of the first stage forward the decode instance’s messages to the same worker of the later stages, so the decode instance and the router address the prefill instance as a pipeline-free one and need no pipeline size.
- It advertises `layer_base_addr_index` (layer name → region index) in the handshake and looks the peer's layers up by name. A peer without the field is only used when it registered the same number of regions, and otherwise the transfer fails with an error that names both counts.
- It sends `write_done` with `sender = [pp_rank, tp_rank]` and `num_writers` multiplied by `pp_size`. The decode rank counts distinct senders and marks the transfer settled, so late or repeated reports are dropped. Messages without a sender, from older peers, are counted per message, and a single writer's messages don't change.

Pipeline parallelism is only allowed on a WRITE-mode `kv_producer`. A READ-mode decode would have to read each layer from the stage that holds it, and a pipeline-parallel decode would need every producer to address its stages. A stage also refuses a block-outermost KV cache layout, because such a block packs every layer the worker holds, so its stride stops matching the decode's once a stage holds only some of the layers.

Notes:
- Over xGMI, main's completion wait can sleep out the full `transfer_timeout`, or fail with copies still in flight and send no `write_failed`. #64330 fixes the wait and the end-to-end runs were performed with the fix.
- GLM-5.2 and GLM-5.3 layers reuse the sparse-attention top-k of the nearest earlier indexer layer, so on main every pipeline stage must start on a layer that runs its own indexer (for GLM-5.2 at PP4, `VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=22,20,20,16`).

AI agent was used for this PR.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Build DSv4.1 replay builders at warmup and the DSv4/DSv4.1 mono runner at load
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

This PR stops two DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 builds from running inside the first real step, where `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` raises on them. The DSv4.1 decoder-replay attention builders are now built on the first warmup batch. The DSv4/DSv4.1 mono decode runner (peer memory included) is now built at load. Neither site is wrapped in `gpu_sync_allowed()`.

This is part of a 5-PR series that replaces the allow-wrap approach of #64176. In that PR, the review asked for the syncs to be fixed, not allowed. The CI failures by site (https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97758, https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15532):
- **Replay builders** (`indexer.py` `dcp_rank_tensor`): (MI355) DeepSeek V4.1 Mono Decode Numerics and (MI300) DeepSeek V4.1 gfx942 Mono Decode Layers.
- **Mono runner** (`peer_memory.py:93`): only (MI355) DeepSeek V4 Pro Mono Decode Numerics, in `test_dsv4_mono_layers.py` at TP8. The DSv4.1 mono-runner sync never showed in CI, because the replay-builder failure came first; it was reproduced locally (see Validation).

The follow-up PR that wraps the test-only probe hooks and turns `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` back on in `docker/Dockerfile.rocm` depends on this PR.

## Claims

- **DSv4.1 replay builders.** `DeepseekV41ModelState` built its copies of the decoder-replay attention groups lazily, in the first eager prefill step that trims a request to the SWA window. That runs every metadata builder's `__init__`, and the indexer builder's `dcp_rank_tensor = torch.tensor(..., device=...)` is a blocking H2D copy inside `execute_model`. The copies are now built on the first `prepare_attn` call, a warmup batch, for every config (before, only PCP>1 did this).
- **Mono runner at load.** The runner was built in the first decode step that took the mono path: IPC heap allocation, gloo handle exchange, `tp_agree`, and the blocking H2D copy of the peer addresses at `peer_memory.py:93`. It is now built in `process_weights_after_loading`, where every TP rank processes the same layers in the same order. For DSv4-Pro the layer's weights are also taken there, which moves the `torch.equal` check in `_scale_bytes` out of the step too.
- **No intended numeric change.** The same builders, runner and weights are built, only earlier. Eager greedy tokens match base token for token (see Validation).
- **CUDA is affected too.** `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model_state.py` is shared by CUDA and ROCm, and CUDA eager mode took the same in-step builder construction.

## Validation

All runs used MI355X (gfx950), ROCm torch 2.13 and amd-aiter 0.1.28.post1.

| Check | Base | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| New unit test `test_replay_builders_built_before_first_trimmed_step` | fails at `tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py:165`: `assert (None is None and 0 == 2)` | passes |
| E2E DSv4.1 replay repro, `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, eager, TP1, mxfp4 indexer | `RuntimeError: GPU<->CPU sync detected` at `indexer.py` `dcp_rank_tensor` (same traceback as CI) | passes; also with the FP8 indexer (block 64, the gfx942 config) and with CUDA graphs plus decoder-replay graph capture |
| Eager greedy tokens, 4 prompts of 300-1203 tokens x 8 tokens | reference (base, `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=warn`) | identical, token for token (mxfp4 and fp8 indexers) |
| E2E DSv4.1-Flash, 5 layers, dummy weights, TP2, `--monokernel`, eager, `enable_extensible_kv_cache=False`, `max_num_seqs=64` (so no warmup batch fits DSv4.1's 48-row mono limit), `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` | base = `main` with the replay-builder site temporarily wrapped in `gpu_sync_allowed()` to get past it: exit 1, sync at `peer_memory.py:93` via `mono_decode.py` `_mono_runner` | exit 0, mono layer active inside the checked steps, no sync detected |
| `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py::test_mono_decode_matches_the_model[2-8]`, `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, TP2. Ran on the stacked series (all five PRs' fixes plus the probe-hook wrap; this PR's code there is identical apart from comment wording) | n/a | 1 passed (127 s); it would raise on any sync, and the log has no `sync detected` line |

**Partial, to be completed before leaving draft: DSv4-Pro at TP8.** `tests/models/test_dsv4_mono_layers.py` (the only CI job that hit `peer_memory.py:93`) uses random weights and only the cached DeepSeek-V4-Pro config, but needs TP8 (the kernels require `TP_SIZE=8`). One attempt on this branch plus the probe-hook commit from #64176, under `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`: the first (mono-on) engine logged `DSv4 mono decode layer active (decode steps of <= 64 rows)` and generated all 8 prompts with no sync detected; the second (mono-off reference) engine then failed in KV-cache sizing (`No available memory for the cache blocks`) because other jobs on the shared host took GPU memory mid-run, so the mono-vs-reference comparison did not complete. To finish (tree: this branch plus the probe-hook commit; base: `main` plus only that commit):

```bash
cd tests && VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 \
  python -m pytest -v -s models/test_dsv4_mono_layers.py
```

On current `main` the base is expected to pass too, because #62560's sampler warmup (`max_num_seqs=8`) builds the runner before the sync check (see Details), so this run checks that the PR does not regress the DSv4-Pro path rather than reproducing the CI failure.

The replay-builder fix alone is what lets the TP2 test get past its first prefill. Whether it also exercises the DSv4.1 mono at-load path depends on warmup (its `max_num_seqs` is within DSv4.1's 48-row limit, so on current `main` the sampler warmup builds the runner anyway); the `max_num_seqs=64` E2E row is the direct evidence for the DSv4.1 mono runner.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
# Unit tests on this branch: 147 passed, 2 skipped (test_deepseek_v41_pcp needs 8 GPUs)
cd tests && HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=5 python -m pytest -q \
  models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_start.py \
  models/test_deepseek_v41_decoder_replay_layers.py models/test_deepseek_v41_pcp.py \
  models/test_deepseek_v41_amd_replay_forward.py models/test_dsv4_mono_decode.py \
  models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py
```

Earlier, without the sync check, `test_dsv41_mono_layers.py`, `test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py`, `test_dsv4_mono_layers.py` and `test_dsv4_mono_numerics.py` were run on 2 GPUs: 3 passed, 9 skipped (the skipped cases need 4 or 8 GPUs, or gfx942).

`pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks pass.
</details>

**Model evaluation.** None was run. The change only moves when the same objects are constructed and does not touch any kernel or math path. Eager greedy outputs are token-identical to base, and the per-layer mono-vs-reference test `test_dsv41_mono_layers[2-8]` passes; the DSv4-Pro one is pending (above).

**Not covered locally:**
- **gfx942 / MI300** and the **DSv4.1 TP4** mono tests were not run. The gfx942 config was only covered by the TP1 FP8-indexer replay repro above.
- **DSpark draft runner:** it is now built at the draft model's load, but no DSpark speculative run was done.

## Details

**Root cause: replay builders.** Warmup dummy batches never trim, so `_prepare_replay_batch` skipped the lazy copy during warmup, and the first real trimmed eager prefill built every replay builder inside `execute_model`. With CUDA graphs, the replay-graph capture happened to build the copies at warmup, which hid the problem; the mono CI tests run with `enforce_eager=True`. The fix:
- `prepare_attn` builds the copies on its first call, for every config. In eager MRV2 without JIT warmup or the extensible KV cache, that first call is the sampler warmup's dummy run (#62560), before `enable_gpu_sync_check`.
- `capture_inner_cudagraphs` rebuilds the copies from the real groups instead of dropping them, because `profile_only` captures run on the pre-KV-cache groups.
- `_prepare_replay_batch` asserts that the copies exist instead of building them.

**Root cause: mono runner.** The runner depends only on the TP group, the rank, the device and static config; whether a warmup step built it first depended on the tree and the configuration. The failing CI job ran a tree (`a85566cc9`, 2026-10-28) from before #62560, which added the MRV2 sampler warmup dummy run. In that tree, an eager MRV2 run with `enable_jit_warmup=False` and no extensible KV cache (the CI config: `max_num_seqs=8`) ran no warmup forward with attention metadata (the profile run skips attention), so the first real decode step built the runner. Since #62560 (2026-11-02), the sampler warmup's dummy batch of `max_num_seqs` one-token requests is decode-only and builds the runner when `max_num_seqs` is within the mono kernels' row limit (48 for DSv4.1, 64 for DSv4-Pro), so by code reading (not yet run) the CI config no longer reproduces on current `main`; with more rows than that (the local DSv4.1 repro uses 64), or on a non-last PP rank, the first real decode step still builds it. The runner is now built at load:
- **DSv4.1:** a new `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer.process_weights_after_loading` builds the target runner, or the draft runner for DSpark draft layers. `finalize_model_weights` runs it children-first in a fixed order, so the gloo handshake stays aligned across TP ranks. DSv4.1 `weights()` only takes views and has no sync, so it stays lazy.
- **DSv4-Pro:** the runner and the layer's weights are built at the end of `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM.process_weights_after_loading`, after the attn/gate_up preshuffle, because the weights need the preshuffled scales.
- The lazy build in `_mono_runner` stays as a fallback for direct callers such as the unit tests.

**Tradeoffs and limitations:**
- The mono IPC heap and runner buffers are now allocated at load, so the KV-cache sizing counts them. Before, they appeared after KV sizing.
- Eager non-PCP configs now always build the replay builder copies, and their device buffers, at warmup. CUDA-graph mode and PCP>1 already did. The cost is small and fixed.
- In graph mode the copies are built at the first capture `prepare_attn` and rebuilt in `capture_inner_cudagraphs`: a transient double construction, at warmup only.
- **Non-last PP ranks:** the MRV2 sampler warmup runs only on the last PP rank. On other ranks in eager mode without JIT warmup or the extensible KV cache, the first `prepare_attn` (and so the replay builders, like the existing lazy `_replay` upload there) is still a real step. The mono runner is unaffected, as it is built at load.
- **Weight reload:** DSv4-Pro `MonoLayerWeights` is still cached and not refreshed on reload, as before. One narrow new case: a weight update before the first decode step (for example a dummy load followed by an RL weight sync) now keeps the scales computed at load; before, they were captured lazily after the update.
- **Sleep mode (not verified):** with `--enable-sleep-mode`, the runner's torch-allocated buffers (for example `PeerBuffer.addresses`) are now allocated during load and may land in the CuMem `weights` pool. Level 2 sleep discards that pool, and the cached runner is not rebuilt on wake-up, so its buffers could hold stale data. Before, they were allocated at step time, outside the tagged pool. `--monokernel` with sleep level 2 should be treated as unsupported until checked.
- **Runner device:** it is taken from `attn_norm.weight.device`; before, from the activation's device. These are the same unless decoder-layer weights are CPU/UVA-offloaded.
- **Other models:** MiniMax-M3 and Kimi-K3 use a similar `PeerBuffer` build-in-step pattern. They did not fail in CI and are out of scope here.

**Duplicate-work check.** I searched open PRs for `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK`, `gpu_sync_allowed`, sync rocm, and each site's keywords (`dcp_rank_tensor`, `_replay_attn_groups`, mono runner, `PeerBuffer`). No other open PR addresses these sites. #64176 is the submitter's own predecessor, which wrapped them in `gpu_sync_allowed()`; this series replaces that approach. #66003 removes a different allowed sync in the `ROCM_AITER_FA` builder and does not overlap.

**AI assistance.** AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate, implement, validate and write this description.

commits.pr_title: [Core][Bugfix] Run the warmup dummy forward on every PP rank before the GPU sync check
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Run the post-capture warmup dummy forward on every PP rank before `enable_gpu_sync_check()`; keep the sampler warmup on the last rank. Follow-up requested in the review of #66397; needed before #64176 turns `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` back on for AMD CI.

## Claims

- `gpu_worker.py`: `_compile_or_warm_up_model` runs the attention-bearing `_dummy_run(max_num_reqs)` on every non-pooling PP rank; only the last rank then runs `_dummy_sampler_run`.
- `test_gpu_worker.py`: a non-last and a last PP rank both run a forward before the sync check, and only the last rank runs the sampler. The non-last case fails on `main`.

## Validation

MI350X (gfx950), PP=2, TP=1, eager, `enable_extensible_kv_cache=False`, `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`:

| Check | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-0.6B with a probe worker extension whose first attention-metadata build does a blocking H2D copy (the pattern of the DSv4.1 indexer's `dcp_rank_tensor`) | PP rank 0 had 0 metadata builds before the check, then raised `GPU<->CPU sync detected` in its first `execute_model` | both ranks built before the check; 10/10 runs, no sync |
| New unit test | non-last case fails | passes |
| `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py` + `tests/utils_/test_gpu_sync_debug.py` | | 73 passed |
| `tests/distributed/test_pp_cudagraph.py`, `test_pipeline_parallel.py -k "mp and not Phi-3.5-MoE or mixed_precision"` (2 GPUs) | | 10 passed, 6 skipped |

## Details

On `main`, the dummy forward right before `enable_gpu_sync_check()` runs only on the last PP rank, because it came in with the sampler warmup (#62560). With eager mode, JIT warmup off and the extensible KV cache off, nothing else gives the other ranks an attention-bearing forward before the check (the profile run skips attention), so anything built lazily on the first forward is built inside the first checked step and raises there.

No in-tree model is known to hit this today: Qwen3-0.6B, DeepSeek-V2-Lite, Nemotron-3-Nano and mamba-130m pass on plain `main` in this configuration, and DSv4.1 is covered already (decoder replay only runs on the last stage, and the DSv4 sparse-MLA warmup runs a forward on every rank). The reproduction above uses a probe to show the ordering gap; this change closes it before the check is enabled rather than fixing an observed model failure. Cost: one extra `max_num_reqs` forward on non-last ranks at startup (PP rank 0's CUDA-graph build count goes from 22 to 23); startup time stayed within noise.

It does not depend on #66397 and can land independently. Not a duplicate: the only open PR touching PP warmup, #54630, changes the seeded sampler pass in `gpu/warmup.py`.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Fix stale W4A16 intermediate_pad expectation in AITER MXFP4 padding test
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`test_aiter_moe_padding_matrix_mxfp4[{intermediate,both}-mxfp4_w4a16]` fails on every AMD nightly since #61816, which made AITER MXFP4 W4A16 forward `intermediate_pad=0` when there is no bias. The test still expects 512 (from #62996). Latest failing job: https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15795/list?jid=01a1bfc2-107b-4b48-af4c-07b32a58f677

## Claims

- Fixes the 2 failing W4A16 cases on MI355, MoE Kernels Shards 2 and 4 (`forwarded intermediate_pad=0, expected 512`).
- Test-only change: no change to `rocm_aiter_moe.py` or to the W4A4 cases.

## Validation

MI355 (gfx950), main @ f86a3e29d7:
```
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 pytest -v \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_modular_kernel_combinations.py::test_aiter_moe_padding_matrix_mxfp4
```
Before: 2 failed, 6 passed. After: 8 passed, including the numerical check against the unpadded reference.

## Details

#61816 changed `rocm_aiter_fused_experts()` in two ways. It stopped doubling the W4A16 pad, and it forwards `intermediate_pad=0` for bias-less, non-SITU W4A16, because AITER's FlyDSL stage 1 leaves the padded intermediate columns unwritten (ROCm/aiter#6598). The padding-matrix test builds its weights without a bias, so 0 is the correct value. The expected constant was never updated. 
Last green nightly: https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15785, 
first red: https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15787.

commits.pr_title: [Refactor][SleepMode] Make CuMemAllocator helpers overridable
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Move the six allocator helpers into `CuMemAllocator` as private, overridable methods so subclasses can reuse its allocation lifecycle methods.

## Claims

- Make `_create_and_map`, `_unmap_and_release`, `_create_cpu_backup`, and `_release_cpu_backup` private static methods, with internal calls dispatched through `self`.
- Make `_get_pluggable_allocator` and `_use_memory_pool_with_allocator` private instance methods that use the existing retained callbacks.
- Update both poisoned-remapping test helpers to replace and restore the class static method correctly.

## Validation

The human submitter reviewed the initial migration and published [CUDA verification for head `47849d33b5`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/66518#issuecomment-6737469715), covering the allocator/sleep suites, HTTP sleep interfaces, subclass dispatch, and a baseline comparison. The report explicitly leaves ROCm, XPU, and downstream Ascend unverified. These device results are submitter-reported; the agent's Windows host has PyTorch 2.13.0+cpu and cannot reproduce them. Agent-side checks for the `_` prefix revision included an exact rename-only AST comparison, actual module/constructor/descriptor checks, applicable commit hooks, and mypy on both test files.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/basic_correctness/memory/cumem/test_cumem.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/basic_correctness/memory/sleep_mode/test_sleep_mode.py -v
```

The subsequent review fix documents the subclassing contract and returns the pluggable allocator directly. Ruff, formatting, applicable commit hooks, source compilation, real module import/construction, and an AST comparison limited to the docstring and immediate-return simplification passed. Device tests were not rerun for this follow-up. The preceding head `47849d33b5` also has a [published device verification report](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/66518#issuecomment-6737469715).

Agent-side checks:

- Ruff 0.17.2 lint/format, typos, and all ten applicable repository Python check hooks passed, including Buildkite test tethering.
- Module import, the real allocator constructor, compilation of all three changed files, and whitespace checks passed.
- An AST comparison against the base verified unchanged implementations for the four static operations and only callback lookup / helper dispatch changes elsewhere.
- Pinned mypy 1.20.2 passed both test files. The allocator reports three host-environment errors: Unix-only `mmap(flags=...)` / `MAP_PRIVATE`, and the existing nullable library-name annotation. Checking the original file with `--shadow-file` reproduced the same three errors.

Merged #64630 introduced the backup implementation; open #64465 fixes wake-up copy retry and #65772 fixes asleep-allocation backup release. Neither migrates these helpers. commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Render messages for return_prompt_text with reused prompt token ids
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Ignore `kv_transfer_params.prompt_token_ids` on chat requests that set `return_prompt_text`, so `prompt_text` is the rendered prompt instead of `null`. Fixes #66402.

## Claims

- A `/v1/chat/completions` request with `return_prompt_text: true` and forwarded `prompt_token_ids` returns the rendered prompt in `prompt_text`, in both the streaming and the non-streaming path. Before this change it returned `null` with HTTP 200.
- Requests without `return_prompt_text` still reuse the forwarded ids as before.

## Validation

Unit test: extended `test_chat_kv_transfer_prompt_token_ids_ignored_with_echo` to also cover `return_prompt_text`.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py -k ignored_with_echo
```

| | `echo` cases | `return_prompt_text` cases |
|---|---|---|
| `main` (c6b2d6ecbb) | 2 passed | 2 failed |
| this PR | 2 passed | 2 passed |

The full `test_serving_chat.py` gives 214 passed and 10 errors on this PR. All 10 are `TestGPTOSS*` setup errors (`FileNotFoundError: 'vllm'`, the `vllm` binary is not on PATH on my machine); the same error occurs on `main` without this change.

Server test: added `test_kv_transfer_prompt_token_ids_return_prompt_text` to `test_chat_completion.py` next to the existing `kv_transfer_params` round-trip tests. It checks through `RemoteOpenAIServer` that a decode request with forwarded ids returns the same `prompt_text` as the plain request. CI runs it in the `entrypoints-integration-api-server-openai-chat_completion` step.

Run on one H100 80GB with the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-cf5cea2da3` image (10 commits behind this PR's base, none touching `vllm/renderers/` or `chat_completion/`), `Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct`:

```bash
pytest entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_chat_completion.py -k return_prompt_text -v
```

Without the fix:

```text
test_chat_completion.py::test_kv_transfer_prompt_token_ids_return_prompt_text FAILED
E       AssertionError: assert None == '<|im_start|>system\nYou are Qwen, created by Alibaba Cloud. You are a helpful assistant.<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>user\nHello, how are you today?<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\n'
================== 1 failed, 8 deselected in 81.63s (0:01:21) ==================
```

With the fix:

```text
test_chat_completion.py::test_kv_transfer_prompt_token_ids_return_prompt_text PASSED
======================= 1 passed, 8 deselected in 43.78s =======================
```

With `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG`, the server logs `return_prompt_text is set, so messages are rendered instead`, which confirms the server ran the new check.

`pre-commit run ruff-check` and `ruff-format` pass on the changed files.

This change does not affect model output, so no model evaluation was run.

## Details

Root cause: decode-side id reuse (#48145) builds the engine input with `tokens_input(reuse_ids, ...)` and skips the chat template, so the input has no `prompt` text. `AsyncLLM.add_request` takes the request's prompt text from that input's `prompt` key, and `chat_completion/serving.py` returns it as `prompt_text`, so it is `None`. #55771 fixed the same conflict for `echo` and media by ignoring the ids and rendering `messages`; this PR adds `return_prompt_text` to that check in `_reused_prompt_token_ids`.

Flow on a P/D decode request:
1. The decode request arrives with `messages`, `return_prompt_text: true` and `kv_transfer_params.prompt_token_ids`.
2. `preprocess_chat` calls `_reused_prompt_token_ids`, which now returns `None`, so `messages` is rendered as on a request without forwarded ids.
3. The ids are still popped from `kv_transfer_params`, so they stay out of the engine's sampling metadata, and the KV transfer proceeds unchanged.

Tradeoff: these requests pay for chat templating and tokenization again on decode. That is the cost `return_prompt_text` needs, since the field returns that rendered text.

Both callers of `_reused_prompt_token_ids` (`preprocess_chat` and the Harmony chat path) read the flag from the request, so both are covered. `docs/features/disagg_prefill.md` lists `return_prompt_text` with `echo` and non-text content as the cases where the ids are ignored.

Not a duplicate: open PRs #64721 and #62333 change `_reused_prompt_token_ids`, but neither handles `return_prompt_text`.

AI assistance was used to trace the code path and draft the change; I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

commits.pr_title: [Recipe][ROCm] MiniMax-M3.1-Flash MI355X AgentX PD disaggregation over MoRI-IO
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Adds `mi355x_agentx_pd`, an opt-in MI355X `pd_cluster` preset to the MiniMax-M3.1-Flash recipe. One TP4 prefill engine feeds two TP4 decode engines over MoRI-IO RDMA WRITE (1P2D, 12 GPUs). It runs at AgentX concurrency 40-128 on the image and opt-in ROCm switches of `mi355x_agentx` (#66188), and needs #65822.

## Claims

- Six concurrency points (40, 48, 64, 96, 112, 128), each with its own decode batch cap, decode CUDA graph sizes and prefill host-DRAM KV size.
- At equal p90 interactivity, 6-32% more total tokens/s per GPU than the aggregated TP4 lane of SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#4866.
- The JSON API differs from main only by this preset.

## Validation

`validate-source.mjs --source vllm` (vllm-project/recipes @ 3360c23) passes. Each point's rendered command matches its run's launch argv, except block rejection for the benchmark's synthetic rejection and builder-owned ports. Single 3600 s agentx-harness 1.0.12 runs in ROCm/ATOM CI; no accuracy evaluation on this configuration.

<details><summary>Results</summary>

Image `nightly-4fab5a07` with the Python files of #65822 overlaid (concurrency 96: #65822 and #63483, DBO off); synthetic rejection at acceptance length 4.04.

| Concurrency | ATOM run | tok/s/GPU | Interactivity p50 / p90 | TTFT p90 | #4866 at same p90 | Delta |
| ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 40 | [42381254638](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/42381254638) | 24,884 | 312.7 / 241.0 | 0.8 s | 23,463 | +6.1% |
| 48 | [42368333455](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/42368333455) | 29,553 | 277.3 / 229.9 | 1.1 s | 25,054 | +18.0% |
| 64 | [42367599740](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/42367599740) | 39,616 | 231.5 / 200.4 | 2.4 s | 30,424 | +30.2% |
| 96 | [42340303193](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/42340303193) | 46,295 | 200.7 / 189.0 | 7.1 s | 35,141 | +31.7% |
| 112 | [42367589571](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/42367589571) | 50,561 | 187.0 / 168.4 | 9.6 s | 43,686 | +15.7% |

Every point ran the rendered command. Prefill DBO (#63483) gave the same throughput and interactivity at every point, so the preset leaves it off.

</details>

## Details

The recipe's MI355X pd_cluster block writes NIXL's `--kv-transfer-config` and `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLHNC` by hand. The preset restates MoRI-IO's decode config and sets the default `LBHNC` layout that the runs used; prefill is recomposed by the Simple offload tier. The runbook covers what the builder cannot render: the second decode engine, `consistent_hash` routing and vllm-router >= 0.1.15. No open PR adds an MI355X PD preset here; #65400 touches this file for VR200 only.

commits.pr_title: [Model] Add transcription to the Transformers modeling backend
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Adds `/v1/audio/transcriptions` to the Transformers modeling backend, so VibeVoice-ASR is served without the native implementation in #62398. Needs Transformers 5.23 for `tokenize` on `apply_transcription_request` (huggingface/transformers#49944), and huggingface/transformers#50417 for the sync check, so it stays a draft until those are released.

## Claims

- New `TransformersMultiModalForTranscription`, selected when the HF processor class has `apply_transcription_request`, serves `json`, `text` and `diarized_json`. Also checked through the API: GLM-ASR, Audio Flamingo 3 and `Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-1.7B-hf` transcribe, and Granite Speech has no endpoint.
- `post_process_output` and `parse_diarized_transcript` now take `model_config`, and the latter parses each chunk's raw output, with timestamps shifted by the chunk offset.
- Transcription models measure their audio token limit from the processor, as config values can be per encoder window. Those that don't truncate are sized by the context length up to the audio decode limits (`--limit-mm-per-prompt` changes it), and other audio models keep their budget.
- Different-length audios in one encoder batch no longer crash, and VibeVoice-ASR's `padding_mask` stays on the CPU so that path passes `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` with #50417.

## Validation

B200, bf16, Transformers 5.23.0.dev0. Native numbers are from #62398 on different hardware. The long clips differ: here it is plain WER on 40 min of concatenated LibriSpeech.

| WER | #62398 native | This PR, via the API |
|---|---|---|
| LibriSpeech test-clean, 500 utts | 2.14 % | 2.07 % |
| 40 min, one request | 1.56 % | 1.64 % |

Noise: the backend keeps HF's default VAE sampling, which gave 2.03 % and 2.08 % across two seeds through `LLM` before this rebase. With that default, 5 min at the default limits gave 2.35 %, and 40 min with the three audio limits raised gave 1.58 % at `--max-model-len 32768`, on this PR's code applied to `9b34fec`. `--pipeline-parallel-size 2` gave 2.48 % on 20 LibriSpeech utterances and 2.47 % on 5 min. A LoRA adapter on the text model loads and changes the output, and a zero adapter leaves it unchanged. VoxPopuli-de, cpWER, 60 min, `vllm bench serve` and TP from #62398 were not rerun.

```
vllm serve microsoft/VibeVoice-ASR-HF --dtype bfloat16 --max-model-len 32768 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.5 --seed 0
pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_transformers_audio.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_moss_transcribe_diarize.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_ming_v3_asr.py \
  tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text/transcription/test_transcription_inter_chunk_spacing.py
pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_transformers_audio.py -k "VibeVoice or mixed_lengths"
pytest tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text/transcription/test_transcription_validation.py -k transformers_backend_audio
pytest tests/models/test_initialization.py -k "VibeVoice or TransformersMultiModalForTranscription"
```

All pass (86 passed, 1 xfailed). `test_transformers_audio_mixed_lengths` fails without the fix with `AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'sum'`. Native `Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-1.7B` still transcribes. `MossAudioModel` initialization fails with and without this PR. The tests needing 5.23 skip in CI until the pin is bumped.

## Details

- Streaming returns the raw model output and streamed usage excludes audio tokens (no `get_num_audio_tokens`). `language` is accepted but unused. `translate` raises a `ValueError`, as in #62398.
- Transcripts are not deterministic across seeds, unlike #62398, which uses the VAE mean.
- `diarized_json` needs VibeVoice's or MOSS's segment format, so other models get a 400.
- `Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-1.7B-hf` stays on the native class by default and uses this backend with `--model-impl transformers`.

commits.pr_title: [Doc] Raise the bar for in-tree kernel translation units
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Disclosure

AI assistance was used. The changes were reviewed and tested manually.

## Overview

Each C++ kernel file in `csrc/` is compiled once per GPU architecture, so a file that instantiates every variant of one op can be the whole build's critical path. Six PRs split the worse ones — #63105, #62716, #62717, #62718, #63364, #63365. With them the 9-arch ROCm wheel build goes 85 min 28 s → 472 s, `_rocm_C.abi3.so` 2011.5 → 125.9 MiB, wheel 379 → 266 MiB (#63105, #62921).

Nothing in the repo made that a review criterion, which is what was raised on #63365. This adds `csrc/AGENTS.md` with four rules for kernel translation units, a `§3.5: C++/CUDA Build Cost` checkpoint in the `pr-checklist` skill that asks whether the touched unit is (or is about to become) that critical path, and an entry in the root guide's domain-specific list — the same wiring #62601 used for `tests/AGENTS.md`. The rules are stated once, in the guide. Documentation only: no runtime or build change.

## Claims

- `csrc/AGENTS.md` holds four rules: the per-arch cost model, splitting on the instantiation axis, giving each variant its own symbol and one source of truth for the variant list, and measuring a build-time claim cold.
- The split shape the guide describes is the one already in-tree: hand-written per-variant units (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6c13a380b1b0f071d3522181fb321c5fcd27bfae/csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms_int4.h#L31-L35, #63364), generated units plus generated dispatch (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6c13a380b1b0f071d3522181fb321c5fcd27bfae/csrc/rocm/generate_paged_attn.py#L4-L20, #62716) and their CMake wiring (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6c13a380b1b0f071d3522181fb321c5fcd27bfae/CMakeLists.txt#L1612-L1623).
- `§3.5` gives the trigger and links the guide; `tests/AGENTS.md`, `docs/contributing/incremental_build.md` and the installation docs are untouched.
- Stays inside the budgets of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6c13a380b1b0f071d3522181fb321c5fcd27bfae/docs/contributing/editing-agent-instructions.md#L5-L9: 23 lines for the new guide (limit 300), root guide 163 → 164 (limit 200).

Left to other PRs:
- [ ] A CI check that fails on a unit over some threshold — the code-level counterpart of a doc rule; the threshold depends on the arch list.
- [ ] CUDA-side build numbers: the A/B includes one CUDA PR (#37376), but no CUDA unit was timed.

## Validation

Documentation only, nothing to execute. The A/B below is the evidence behind the guide: ten PRs reviewed twice by a Sonnet reviewer from the same diff, once under `main`'s instructions and once under this PR's. No builds, no tests, no compute: the reviewer reads the diff, restricted to `csrc/` and `CMakeLists.txt`.

| PR | What went into one unit | Cost afterwards | `main` flags build time inflation | This PR flags build time inflation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #8310 | paged attention landed: 128 `paged_attention_ll4mi_QKV` instantiations, block size as a kernel dimension | 71.6 s per unit until #62716 | yes | yes |
| #22222 | fp8 paged attention: an `MFMAType` axis doubling the fp8-KV instantiations of the same unit | 71.6 s per unit until #62716 | yes | yes |
| #42755 | QK-norm + RoPE + KV fusion: `USE_INTERLEAVED_V_CACHE` doubling them again | 71.6 s per unit until #62716 | yes | yes |
| #40860 | DeepSeek V4: `topk_softplus_sqrt_kernels.cu`, ~270 instantiations of the gating kernel, in one unit | 99.7 s of a 102 s build until #62717 | yes | yes |
| #15830 | skinny GEMMs landed as one 1600-line unit, every variant of four kernel families | 58.3 s largest unit until #62718 | no | yes |
| #40687 | the same unit gains one more lane: `case 5` for N=5, two tile configs, in 7 lines | 58.3 s largest unit until #62718 | no | yes |
| #40977 | int4 skinny GEMM dispatch tower: dtypes × zero-point modes × N × tile configs × group sizes in one unit | 1232 s on 9 archs until #63364 | no | yes |
| #57199 | the same tower widened with CHUNKED and `A_CHUNK` instantiations | 1232 s on 9 archs until #63364 | no | yes |
| #62132 | Muse Spark norm fusion: ~400 instantiations of the fused qknorm/rope/kv-insert op in one unit | 478 s on 9 archs until #63365 | yes | yes |
| #37376 | fused qknorm + rope for SM9.0 (CUDA): ~108 instantiations of the new kernel across head dim, interleave, N and dtype | not measured | yes | yes |

`main` flags 6 of the 10, this PR flags 10 of 10. The four it flips are the ones where the inflation is not visible in the diff: a new file that looks like it only pays for itself (#40977: "a separate translation unit, so it doesn't slow the existing `skinny_gemms.cu`" — the new unit was the problem), a 7-line lane addition (#40687: "a small addition I would not raise"), a 1600-line new file (#15830), and a widening of an existing one (#57199). Where `main` already flags, what changes is the answer: an ask to split on the instantiation axis and show a cold `.ninja_log`, instead of "please quantify the build-time impact". The CUDA row (#37376) behaves like the ROCm ones, so the rules are not backend-specific. One sample per cell, one model, no build: a signal, not a measurement.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Metrics] Periodic stats line: dead Preemptions field + Finished count
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The periodic serving-stats line (`Engine 000: Avg prompt throughput: ...`)
could not show preemption churn: the interval counters it reports were
reset before the line was built, so the `Preemptions: N` field
introduced in #28522 never fired, and nothing reported finished-request
counts. This change fixes the ordering and adds an unconditional
`Finished: N reqs` field — `Finished: 0` while generation throughput is
high is the churn signal.

## Changes

- `LoggingStatLogger` now computes throughputs in `_calc_throughput(now)`
  and resets the interval counters *after* the log line is built, so the
  line reads the live counters (`num_preemptions`, `num_corrupted_reqs`,
  `num_finished_reqs`) directly — no snapshot fields.
- `Finished: N reqs` is unconditional: the zero is the diagnostic.
  Prometheus counters are unchanged and already correct; this PR is
  scoped to the human-readable line.
- New `tests/v1/metrics/test_logging_stat_logger.py` covers
  `LoggingStatLogger` through `StatLoggerManager.record()`/`log()`:
  counter accumulate/log/reset, latest-snapshot scheduler values, the
  INFO → two quiet intervals → DEBUG noise policy, the
  Preemptions/Corrupted fields, and the DP-aggregated variant.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/v1/metrics/test_logging_stat_logger.py -v` → 5 passed.
- The same suite against pre-PR `main` fails exactly the bug-guard
  tests (dead `Preemptions` field, missing `Finished` count) and passes

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Reject translation on models that cannot translate
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`/v1/audio/translations` returns a transcript with a 200 on models that cannot translate. These now return a 400, as Ming V3 ASR and Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe already do. Found while checking translation for #65735 and #62398.

## Claims

- Voxtral, Voxtral Realtime, GLM-ASR, Kimi Audio, Cohere ASR, FunASR, FireRedASR2 and MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize raise `ValueError` on `translate`, which the server returns as a 400.
- This is a breaking change for anyone calling `/v1/audio/translations` on these models and using the transcript. `/v1/audio/transcriptions` still works. Kimi Audio and MOSS callers who put an instruction in `prompt` can send it there instead.
- Unrelated small change: the audio upload size error now names `VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_CLIP_FILESIZE_MB`, as the decode limit errors already name theirs.

## Validation

B200, Transformers 5.23.0.dev0, `temperature=0`, `/v1/audio/translations` with `language=en`.

| Model | Before, `to_language=de` | After |
|---|---|---|
| `zai-org/GLM-ASR-Nano-2512` | 200, English | 400 |
| `mistralai/Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507` | 200, English | 400 |
| `Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-1.7B` | 200, mostly German | Unchanged |
| `ibm-granite/granite-speech-3.3-2b` | 200, English then German | Unchanged |

GLM-ASR and Voxtral also returned Italian for Italian audio with `to_language=en`, where `openai/whisper-small` translated. Transcription still returns 200 on all four.

```
pytest tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text/translation/test_translation_validation.py -k transcription_only
```

1 passed through `RemoteOpenAIServer`. The test itself was not run without the fix, but the same request returned 200 before it. Those runs used this patch on `9b34fec`. Pre-commit passes.

## Details

- GLM-ASR had a translate prompt, but the model ignores it. The others never read the task, so their prompt is the same as for transcription.
- Only GLM-ASR and Voxtral were run. Kimi Audio, Cohere ASR, FunASR, FireRedASR2 and Voxtral Realtime were not run: I called each `get_generation_prompt` directly and confirmed it raises. MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize was checked the same way, because it failed at startup on this environment with `KeyError: 'padding_mask'`, before reaching this code.
- Gemma 3n was not run (`timm` missing), and the existing translation tests cover it. Canary and Qwen3-Omni were not run and are unchanged.

No open PR or issue covers this: searched open PRs and issues for translation on these endpoints.

commits.pr_title: [Feature][KV Offload] Add RDMA-capable OBJ tier (#55855)
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #55855.

Lets the KV offload OBJ secondary tier use NIXL's accelerated (S3-over-RDMA) object-store engines, pinned to NIXL 1.5.2.

- Accelerated NIXL OBJ options (`accelerated`, `type`, `use_virtual_addressing`, `req_checksum`, `resp_checksum`) are passed through `store_config.backend_params`. No new `ObjStoreConfig` fields. Connection fields and `num_threads` stay
reserved and cannot be overridden. Bool values are normalized to `"true"`/`"false"`.
- The primary CPU DRAM pool is registered in chunks of at most `4 GiB - 64 KiB`. cuObject-based engines reject larger registrations: `CUOBJ_MAX_MEMORY_REG_SIZE` is 4 GiB in the CUDA 13.2 header and 4 GiB - 64 KiB in 13.3. Without this, a CPU
tier above 4 GiB fails at startup. A single block larger than the limit raises a clear `ValueError`.
- Docs: `backend_params` row and an accelerated example in `kv_offloading_usage.md`.

Not duplicating #65956: that PR is about <fill in the actual scope>. This one only adds the `backend_params` passthrough and the chunked DRAM registration, which that PR does not touch. <Confirm before posting.>

Scope note: NIXL 1.5.2 ships only a vendor engine (`type: dell`). With `accelerated: true` and no `type`, it initializes an accelerated client that still transfers over plain S3. The generic S3-RDMA engine is on NIXL main / 1.6 and is not
covered here.

## Test Plan

Unit tests:

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_obj_tier.py -v
```

End to end on 1x L40S (Qwen2.5-0.5B, `TieringOffloadingSpec`, `block_size` 64, 40 distinct prompts of about 3.5k tokens, FlashBlade S3 over plain HTTP, NIXL 1.5.2):

1. Cold run, then GPU prefix-cache hit.
2. `POST /reset_prefix_cache?reset_external=true`, then replay.
3. Integrity check: output of the GPU hit must equal output of the OBJ-tier reload. (Cold vs. warm differs by prefill numerics even on plain vLLM, so it is not the reference.)
4. NIC counters (`rx_write_requests` on the mlx5 device and netdev bytes) before and after, to distinguish RDMA from TCP.
5. 9 GiB CPU tier, to exercise the chunked registration.

## Test Result

- `test_obj_tier.py`: 50 passed.
- `test_model_tensor_schema[baidu/Unlimited-OCR]` (earlier CI failure, `'dict' object has no attribute 'projector_type'`): fails on the pre-merge commit, passes after merging main (GPU run). The 3
`test_processing_correctness[...Unlimited-OCR]` variants pass on both trees locally, so I could not reproduce those.

| Path | GPU hit vs OBJ reload | `rx_write_requests` delta | Netdev RX |
|---|---|---|---|
| standard S3 | identical (0/40 differ) | 0 | 1656 MiB |
| `accelerated: true`, no `type` (NIXL 1.5.2) | identical (0/40 differ) | 0 | 1656 MiB |
| `accelerated: true` + `type`, S3-RDMA vendor engine (unreleased NIXL 1.5.2 plugin build, test only) | identical (0/40 differ) | 4400 | 4 MiB |

- 1.6 GiB of KV was served from the object tier in each run (140,800 external prefix-cache tokens).
- The RDMA engine also passes with a 9 GiB CPU tier through the chunked registration. Control: with chunking disabled, startup fails with `registerMem: region of 9663676416 bytes exceeds CUOBJ_MAX_MEMORY_REG_SIZE`.
- TTFT for this tiny model: cold about 110 ms, GPU hit about 48 ms, OBJ reload about 114 ms (RDMA) / 125 ms (standard S3). Reload is not faster than recompute here, so no TTFT improvement is claimed.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][KV Offload] SimpleCPUOffload: batch copies on SDMA with hipMemcpyFlagExtPreferCE (HIP 7.16+)
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

vLLM's ROCm image now ships the HIP 7.16 runtime (`docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base`, `ROCM_RUNTIME_COMMIT` 25e14349f2). On it, `hipMemcpyBatchAsync` runs `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`'s host <-> device batches as a blit kernel on the CUs (`__amd_rocclr_copyBufferBatch`), so every load or store slows the decode that runs next to it. With `hipMemcpyFlagExtPreferCE` (0x100) in the batch attributes, the runtime hands the whole batch to the SDMA engines instead and no kernel runs.

`build_params` now sets that flag on HIP >= 7.16 (`_copy_flags_for_hip_version`, next to the existing `numAttrs` gate). Older runtimes keep flags 0, so nothing changes for them. CUDA is untouched.

## Claims

- Decode next to the copies: up to +122% slower (median) without the flag, +0.4% to +3.9% with it (table below).
- Copy bandwidth is unchanged: 44-56 GB/s in both directions, alone and under load.
- Round trips stay byte-exact.

## Validation

MI355X, one GPU, image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-40941f2c4ba96fba0a7e282a5355e89cd74d9ac5` (main of 2026-11-03, HIP 7.16.26361). Before = the image's own vLLM (flags 0x0); after = this PR's `cuda_mem_ops.py` copied over it (flags 0x100); same job, same GPU. The copies go through `build_params` + `copy_blocks` exactly as the connector calls them, on one TP4 rank's KV layout of a 60-layer model: 131 per-layer tensors, 16 / 32 KiB pages (3.09 MiB per block), a registered host buffer, shuffled block ids, a low-priority stream. Decode is a CUDA graph of 32 bf16 GEMMs (M x 6144 x 4096 and back, 1.5 GiB of distinct weights, HBM-bound) replayed while N-block transfers loop; slowdown = per-replay time vs the same graph alone.

| M | direction | N blocks | decode slowdown before: median (mean, p99) | after: median (mean, p99) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16 | load | 32 | +27.3% (+93.9%, +196%) | **+3.6%** (+3.3%, +6%) |
| 16 | load | 128 | +3.7% (+46.2%, +455%) | **+3.9%** (+3.6%, +6%) |
| 16 | store | 32 | +88.2% (+98.3%, +327%) | **+0.5%** (+0.5%, +2%) |
| 16 | store | 128 | +0.6% (+55.6%, +464%) | **+0.6%** (+0.6%, +2%) |
| 64 | load | 32 | +121.5% (+75.6%, +132%) | **+1.3%** (+1.2%, +2%) |
| 64 | load | 128 | +1.8% (+43.4%, +328%) | **+1.5%** (+1.4%, +2%) |
| 64 | store | 32 | +114.4% (+65.1%, +119%) | **+0.4%** (+0.4%, +1%) |
| 64 | store | 128 | +0.7% (+43.0%, +338%) | **+0.4%** (+0.4%, +1%) |

Without the flag the slowdown is bimodal: some replays are clean and the rest (10-78% of them, depending on the row) run 1.2x to 5.6x slower, so some medians look fine while the means and tails do not. With the flag no replay is more than 1.2x slower.

- Copy bandwidth, before -> after: load 44.2-55.5 -> 44.1-55.6 GB/s, store 44.7-54.7 -> 44.1-55.1 GB/s (8-512 blocks, alone).
- Byte-exact round trip (64 random blocks x 131 tensors, GPU -> CPU -> other GPU blocks): 0 differing tensors before and after.
- `pytest tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_hip_mem_ops.py`: the new `test_copy_flags_for_hip_version` covers the gate (unknown, ROCm 7.2, HIP 7.15, 7.16, 8.0); like the rest of that file it needs no HIP runtime.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend][Perf] Reduce per-request output channel memory
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Rust frontend creates one Tokio output channel for every active
request. Each channel currently stores 304-byte output deliveries inline,
causing a drained but warmed channel to retain about 22.5 KB of memory.

Store queued deliveries behind `Box` pointers and unwrap them at the
receiver boundary. The output type, ordering, error propagation, and
stream behavior remain unchanged.



## Claims

- Reduces the Tokio channel slot size from 304 bytes to 8 bytes on
  64-bit platforms.
- Reduces measured warmed-channel RSS from about 22.5 KB to 1.6 KB per
  active request.
- Preserves the existing output stream API and wire behavior.
- Keeps the implementation private to the per-request output channel.

The total memory savings increase with the number of concurrently active
request streams.



## Validation
```
cargo nextest run -p vllm-engine-core-client --all-features
cargo clippy -p vllm-engine-core-client --all-targets  --all-features --locked  -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --all -- --check
```

A release-mode microbenchmark repeatedly sent and drained outputs across
independent channels. Each scenario was run three times in a separate
process, and the median result is reported below.

| Queue item | RSS per channel | Change |
|---|---:|---:|
| Inline Result<Delivery> | 22,523.1 bytes | Baseline |
| Boxed Result<Delivery> | 1,572.9 bytes | -93.0% |



## Details

Tokio's unbounded MPSC channel stores messages in blocks containing 32
slots. With a 304-byte delivery, each block reserves space for 32 complete
delivery values. Warming the channel can leave reusable blocks allocated
even after all queued messages have been consumed.

Boxing the queued value makes each channel slot pointer-sized. A private
receiver wrapper delegates to Tokio's existing poll_recv implementation
and immediately unwraps the value, so downstream consumers continue to
receive Result<EngineCoreStreamDelivery>.

Boxing adds one heap allocation per queued delivery in exchange for
substantially smaller channel blocks. The change is limited to internal
queue storage and does not alter externally observable behavior.
