commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Qwen3.5] Replace FlashInfer GemmaRMSNorm JIT with Triton for arch<sm80
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Qwen3.5's RMSNorm no longer JIT-compiles FlashInfer kernels on sm75 (T4). Fixes #66288.

## Claims

- Qwen3.5 starts on sm75 without building the FlashInfer `norm` module (previously a ~1 min slower cold start, or `Ninja build failed` / `cannot find -lcuda` where nvcc cannot link).
- SM80+ behaviour is unchanged.
- T4 decode is within ~3% of the warm FlashInfer kernel; GSM8K is unchanged.

## Validation

2xT4, Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B, TP=2, `--dtype half`, `--max-model-len 4096`, FlashInfer cache cleared before each server.

`pytest tests/models/qwen3_5/test_rms_norm.py`
- without the fix: 1 failed in 50 s (`Building JIT module norm` -> `cannot find -lcuda` -> `Ninja build failed`)
- with the fix: 2 passed, 2 skipped (bf16 unsupported on T4)

| | FlashInfer norm | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| startup | 139 s (needs a libcuda stub) | 81 s |
| GSM8K (200 q, chat, thinking off) | 0.535 | 0.540 |
| output tok/s (3 runs, 512 in / 128 out, concurrency 8) | 428 / 426 / 420 | 419 / 415 / 412 |
| mean TPOT | 15.0-15.3 ms | 15.4-15.7 ms |

```bash
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --use-chat-completions \
  --max-tokens 512 --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}' --num-questions 200 --seed 42
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 128 --num-prompts 48 --max-concurrency 8
```

`tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py` + `test_qsa_prepare.py` on T4: 44 failed before, 43 after, none newly failing (the remaining failures also occur without this change). The padded-QK test, which hit the same JIT error before, now passes.

Startup times are single cold runs.

## Details

- `Qwen3_5RMSNorm` now subclasses `GemmaRMSNorm`. It uses FlashInfer when `has_device_capability(80) and has_flashinfer()`, otherwise `ir.ops.rms_norm` / `fused_add_rms_norm`.
- The `ir` path passes the Gemma weight `(1 + w)` computed in fp32 and cast to the activation dtype, so the fused vllm_c kernels are selected. The rounding is of the same order as the fp16 output rounding and is within the `ir` test tolerance. With an fp32 weight decode was ~366-372 tok/s.
- The FlashInfer path updates `x` and `residual` in place; the `ir` path returns new tensors. All callers use the returned values.
- `has_flashinfer()` does not detect a missing `flashinfer-jit-cache` on CUDA < 12.9.
- `qsa_indexer.py` (qwen4_exp) now calls its existing `GemmaRMSNorm` modules instead of `flashinfer.norm.gemma_rmsnorm`; the fake norm in `test_qsa_reference.py` is a real `GemmaRMSNorm`.
- CI runs on SM100, so it covers the FlashInfer path; there is no sm75 runner.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Support AITER's preload() in FlyDSL INT4 QuickReduce init
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Since #65937 (merged 2026-11-06) vLLM main pins AITER v0.1.28.post1, and with it every ROCm worker dies at start-up when INT4 QuickReduce is on, because ROCm/aiter#5461 renamed `QuickAllReduceInt4.compile()` to `preload()`; this calls `preload()` when `compile()` is gone. #65628 carries the same check inside a larger feature PR; this is the standalone fix, co-authored with @eppaneamd.

## Claims

- ROCm serving with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, `VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4` and TP > 1 starts again on AITER with #5461.
- No change on AITER without #5461 (v0.1.27 and older): the `compile()` branch runs as before.

## Validation

**Reproduction** (vLLM main + AITER main `20455aa6`, which has #5461; MI355X, TP4). Any TP > 1 server with these two variables hits the same init path; the exact command run is below.

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 \
vllm serve amd/GLM-5.3-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8 --tensor-parallel-size 4 ...
```

```
File ".../device_communicators/quick_all_reduce.py", line 280, in _init_flydsl_int4
    flydsl_int4.compile(warmup, torch.empty_like(warmup))
AttributeError: 'QuickAllReduceInt4' object has no attribute 'compile'
```

With this PR, the same server starts and serves (`POST /v1/completions 200`), and every worker logs the FlyDSL path:

```
INFO [quick_all_reduce.py:289] Using AITER FlyDSL INT4 QuickReduce for BF16 payloads; other payloads use the HIP QuickReduce kernels.
```

**Unit test**: `pytest tests/distributed/test_rocm_quick_reduce.py -k "flydsl_int4 or two_gpu_correctness"`, 2x MI355X (gfx950), vLLM nightly `a2bcb565`:

| AITER | Without this PR | With this PR |
|---|---|---|
| main `20455aa6` (has `preload()`) | 1 failed, 4 passed (`AttributeError` above) | 5 passed |
| `269675de` (has `compile()`, before #5461) | 5 passed | 5 passed |

The new case `test_quick_allreduce_two_gpu_flydsl_int4` asserts the FlyDSL INT4 object was built (the path under test ran, not the HIP fallback) and checks a BF16 all-reduce result.

<details>
<summary>Full server command</summary>

```bash
SAFETENSORS_FAST_GPU=1 VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MOE_DISPATCH_POLICY=0 VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MHA=0 \
AITER_USE_FLYDSL_MOE_SORTING=1 AITER_DISABLE_FLYDSL_TOPK_DECODE=1 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 \
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS=0 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4BMM=0 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA=1 AITER_FLYDSL_STAGE2_FP8=1 \
vllm serve amd/GLM-5.3-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --trust-remote-code \
  --max-model-len 262144 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 \
  --max-num-seqs 256 --enable-chunked-prefill --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --compilation-config '{"pass_config": {"fuse_rope_kvcache_cat_mla": true}, "use_inductor_graph_partition": true}' \
  --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --hf-overrides '{"use_index_cache": true, "index_topk_freq": 4, "index_share_for_mtp_iteration": false}'
```

</details>

## Details

- `compile(inp, out)` built the kernels and ran one all-reduce on every rank, to keep the JIT out of the first prefill and out of CUDA graph capture. `preload()` only builds and loads the kernels (local to the rank), so one warm-up `allreduce()` follows it. Every rank runs this init, so the collective stays matched.
- `hasattr` keeps both AITER versions working; the `compile()` branch can be dropped once the pin is past #5461.
- Arch: only CDNA3/CDNA4 (gfx942, gfx950) reach this code (`is_flydsl_quick_reduce_available`); RDNA, gfx1250, CUDA and AITER-off paths are unchanged.
- Test: one new case in the existing `test_rocm_quick_reduce.py` (the existing two-GPU cases run with AITER off and never reach this init). That file runs in the existing distributed AMD CI step.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Replay one row for far prefill chunks
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

A simpler version of #62817 (DeepSeek-V4.1: replay one row for prefill chunks far from the prompt end). It keeps the original author's commits and adds three commits on top. They drop the model runner hook, the `ModelState` interface method and the MoE finalize change. A config-derived bound replaces them, so the change stays inside `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/`. This is a proposal for #62817, not a competing optimization. If the author prefers, the last three commits can be cherry-picked there and this PR closed.

## Claims

- Same optimization as #62817. A prefill chunk that ends far enough before its prompt's end replays one row, and later chunks never read the rows it skipped.
- No changes to `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`, `model_states/interface.py`, `deepseek_v41/nvidia/model.py` or `decoder_replay_layers.py`.
- Non-test diff vs main: +94/-31 in 3 files (#62817: +172/-38 in 7 files). Tests: +62 (#62817: +136/-2).
- With default settings the same chunks skip their tails as in #62817: 7 of 8 for a 124K prompt in 16K chunks, and 3 of 4 for 64K.

## Validation

Unit tests at this head on GB200: 45 passed.

```bash
pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_decoder_replay_layers.py \
  tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_start.py tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_pcp.py
```

At this head, a test fails when any of these is removed: the tail floor, the replay batch for floored chunks, the last-row clamp, the floor's exact reach, the multimodal gate, or the priority gate.

**Performance on GB300** (measured before the last commit; `vllm bench forward`, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 2xGB300 TP2, dummy weights, median of 5 samples x 20 iters, sample spread <= 0.5%). Each prefill chunk is a non-final one with 8192 prompt tokens still to come, so this PR replays one row where main replays 128. Both arms run on `fac2ce2eb3`, with this PR's diff applied for the second.

| case | main (ms) | this PR (ms) | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16K chunk, first | 141.65 | 135.90 | -5.75 ms (-4.1%) |
| 16K chunk @ 32K | 143.96 | 138.27 | -5.70 ms (-4.0%) |
| 16K chunk @ 64K | 148.88 | 143.14 | -5.73 ms (-3.9%) |

Each skipped tail saves about 5.7 ms, the same as #62817 measured end to end. A 124K prompt in 16K chunks skips 7 tails, which works out to about 40 ms, or roughly -2.2% TTFT (#62817 measured -2.4%).

<details>
<summary>Command</summary>

`bench forward` always treats a prefill case as its prompt's last chunk, so for this A/B only, a local edit appends `BENCH_PROMPT_EXTRA` tokens to each prefill prompt (not part of this PR).

```bash
BENCH_PROMPT_EXTRA=8192 torchrun --nproc-per-node=2 -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main bench forward \
  --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash -tp 2 --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' --language-model-only --max-model-len 131072 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --kv-len-jitter 0 \
  --case first16k=16384 --case mid16k@32k=16384@32768c --case mid16k@64k=16384@65536c \
  --case mid16k@112k=16384@114688c --case mid8k@64k=8192@65536c --case mid4k@64k=4096@65536c \
  --case mid2k@64k=2048@65536c --case 4x4k@32k=4*4096@32768c \
  --case mix8k+32dec=8192@32768c,32*1@8192 --case decode64=64*1@8192
```

</details>

**Performance on GB200 DEP4** (at this head; `vllm bench forward`, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 4xGB200, `-tp 1 -dp 4 --enable-expert-parallel`, dummy weights, 3 samples x 10 iters). The two columns run in one process, alternating. "Rule off" is this PR's code with the rule switched off by a local wrapper (not part of this PR), not main. Cases are per rank. Where two rounds ran with the arm order reversed, the numbers are their mean; the run was stopped early, so the last four rows have one round.

| case | replay rows, rule on | rule off (ms) | rule on (ms) | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16K chunk @ 64K, 8192 tokens to come | 1 | 178.89 | 172.86 | -6.03 ms (-3.4%) |
| 4K chunk @ 64K, 8192 to come | 1 | 57.65 | 51.81 | -5.84 ms (-10.1%) |
| 2K chunk @ 64K, 8192 to come | 1 | 38.12 | 31.99 | -6.13 ms (-16.1%) |
| 4K chunk @ 64K, 1200 to come | 80 | 57.66 | 56.38 | -1.28 ms (-2.2%) |
| 64 tokens @ 64K, 1230 to come | 50 | 14.97 | 14.55 | -0.42 ms (-2.8%) |
| 64 tokens @ 64K, 1150 to come (floored, keeps all rows) | 64 | 14.97 | 15.03 | +0.06 ms (+0.4%) |
| last chunk, 16K @ 64K | 128 | 178.99 | 179.29 | +0.30 ms (+0.2%) |
| last chunk, 1000 tokens @ 64K | 128 | 28.16 | 28.14 | -0.02 ms (-0.1%) |
| last chunk, 100 tokens @ 64K | 100 | 17.15 | 17.16 | +0.01 ms (+0.1%) |
| 4 x 4K chunks @ 32K, 8192 to come | 4 | 182.60 | 172.41 | -10.19 ms (-5.6%) |
| 8K chunk @ 32K + 32 decodes, 8192 to come | 33 | 97.30 | 92.59 | -4.71 ms (-4.8%) |
| 2 ranks 8K chunk @ 64K, 2 ranks 64 decodes | 1 | 127.42 | 124.77 | -2.66 ms (-2.1%) |
| 64 decodes (control) | n/a | 14.19 | 14.16 | -0.04 ms (-0.3%) |

The rule's output is bitwise identical on all ranks for the three last-chunk cases and the decode control. `K` was set to 1280 by the wrapper, because the bench itself runs without graphs. This node's `/dev/shm` was too small for shared Engram tables, so they were DP-sharded. The floored case costs about 0.06 ms in both rounds: it takes the replay batch without trimming, and it only happens to a chunk cut short near the tail.

**Not yet done:** a real-weight end-to-end check (greedy outputs and serving TTFT), and a GB200 DEP4 comparison against main itself. The dummy-weight runs above don't validate real outputs.

## Details

**Why #62817 needs the eager hook.** After a one-row chunk, its skipped rows hold no replay-layer KV. A later chunk whose SWA window reaches back to them must read nothing below them. Only the replay batch's own metadata can apply that floor. In a CUDA graph step that runs the replay layers on the whole batch, they share SWA metadata with the encoder-side layers, so #62817 forces such steps eager from the model runner.

**Why the hook isn't needed.** Such a step can only be a CUDA graph step if it holds at most `max_cudagraph_capture_size` tokens. Neither kind of chunk that can follow a one-row chunk fits in one:

- A chunk whose window reaches back past the replayed tail (`K = max_cudagraph_capture_size + 2 * window` tokens) starts within `window - 1` of it, so if it is the prompt's last chunk it holds more than `max_cudagraph_capture_size + window` tokens.
- A chunk the scheduler cuts short shares its step with at least the smallest prefill cap. That cap is `max_num_scheduled_tokens`, `max_num_batched_tokens - max_num_seqs * draft_slots` (the scheduler takes `draft_slots` off the input budget per request) or `long_prefill_token_threshold`. With adaptive verification, `max_num_seqs * num_speculative_tokens` comes off too, because the runner may drop every draft before it picks a graph. The rule is enabled only when the result exceeds `max_cudagraph_capture_size + window`. That holds by default, because the capture size is at most 1024 and never exceeds `max_num_batched_tokens`.
- The runner sizes graph dispatch from the scheduled token count, which is shrunk only by adaptive verification and PCP (the rule is off under PCP). DP sync only raises it, and ubatching only applies to an already-chosen FULL graph. A future runner feature that shrinks a step before dispatch would have to be added to this bound.
- The second window covers the few tokens that the MTP lookahead or `max_model_len` can shave off a chunk.
- Encoder inputs can cut a chunk anywhere, so the rule is off when the model accepts multimodal inputs. With `--language-model-only` it stays on.

**Other simplifications.**

- Replay batch steps keep holding more than a window of tokens, so the MoE finalize change is not needed.
- The single-use `needs_eager_forward` / `_skipped_tails` helpers are gone.
- The kernel's host-side `kv_floor` (which also drops `_pcp_replay_start`) and the 1..64 replay graph sizes from #62817 are kept.

**What comes from DeepInfer.** The rule follows DeepInfer's [`clip_prefix`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepInfer/blob/a679bb86ce36e883a98a97733492b686e5b9a08e/csrc/engine/input_metadata/prepare_tensor_input_v4.cpp#L203-L231), reimplemented here (no code is copied). A prefill keeps only its rows in the prompt's last K tokens, and always its last row. Those rows read nothing before the last K tokens. Both follow from the prompt length alone, so the model state doesn't track where the last one-row chunk ended.

**What differs from DeepInfer.**

- K is `max_cudagraph_capture_size + 2 * window`, not DeepInfer's 140 (window + backtracking). vLLM can run a small prefill chunk in a whole-batch graph, where no floor applies, so a chunk that reads back past the tail must be too large for a graph. Chunks ending within K of the prompt's end keep their full window, which costs one extra replay tail on some prompts.
- A one-row chunk reads itself and writes its KV, which nothing reads. DeepInfer's placeholder row reads nothing and doesn't write.
- The first replay layer still reads its full window, and the last window's floor stays `seq_len - window` as on main. So outputs are not meant to match DeepInfer bit for bit.
- The rule is off under PCP. DeepInfer's CP boundary redistribution isn't ported.
- Prompt-logprob requests keep every row. DeepInfer turns prompt logprobs off instead.

**Tradeoff.** Unlike #62817, the rule is off when `long_prefill_token_threshold` or another prefill cap is at most the capture size plus a window, when multimodal inputs are enabled, or when the scheduling policy is priority, where preemption can return a step's budget after a chunk was cut short. Those deployments keep today's behavior.

commits.pr_title: [CI][ROCm] Mirror LM Eval ReplaySSM on MI355
commits.pr_body:
- `lm_eval.yaml`: add an AMD mirror (MI355, 2 GPUs) to `lm-eval-replayssm-2xb200`.
- `models-mi355-replayssm.txt` + `Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-FP8-ReplaySSM-align-MI355.yaml`: GSM8K config for Nemotron-3-Super with `--use-replayssm` on the Triton Mamba backend, TP2 + EP, prefix caching, V2 model runner.

The B200 ReplaySSM nightly had no AMD counterpart, so nothing on AMD CI exercised the Triton ReplaySSM decode kernel (`selective_state_update_replayssm_output_only`) end to end. The mirror runs the same GSM8K check with the same 0.93 threshold and the same `expect_prefix_cache_hits` check. It uses the ROCm backends from the existing MI355 Nemotron-3-Super configs (AITER, Triton MoE, `ROCM_AITER_FA`), and the FP8 checkpoint instead of NVFP4. Two parts of the B200 config are left out because main does not support them on the Triton backend: MTP, because `VllmConfig` rejects Mamba2 ReplaySSM speculative decoding unless `--mamba-backend flashinfer`, and stochastic rounding, which uses the CUDA-only `cvt.rs` PTX instruction. `--prefix-match-unit` is 608 instead of 327 because the hybrid page here is 4864 tokens. 608 divides that and fits inside the 663-token shared few-shot prefix. `--mamba-cache-mode align` is dropped because it is deprecated and has no effect on main, since prefix caching already sets align mode. The mirror's source dependencies add the Triton ReplaySSM kernel and `rocm.py`.

No open PR adds an AMD mirror for this step. I searched open PRs for "ReplaySSM AMD", "ReplaySSM ROCm", "ReplaySSM MI355", "LM Eval ReplaySSM", "replayssm mirror" and "Nemotron-3-Super ReplaySSM". #66207 changes the B200 NVFP4 config (`--block-size 16`), not this one. #63918 changes the tf32x3 gate for non-ROCm platforms and does not change ROCm behaviour.

### Validation

MI350X (gfx950), 2 GPUs, the exact mirror command:

```bash
cd tests
export VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn
pytest -s -v evals/gsm8k/test_gsm8k_correctness.py --config-list-file=configs/models-mi355-replayssm.txt
```

| | Runs | GSM8K (threshold 0.93) | Prefix-cache hit tokens |
|---|---|---|---|
| ReplaySSM config, 10 runs in a row | 10/10 passed | 0.9265-0.9386, mean 0.9327 | 801,344 every run |
| Rebased on current main, 1 run | passed | 0.9371 | 801,344 |
| Same config without `--use-replayssm` (unit 528 for its 4224-token page) | 1 run, passed | 0.9348 | - |

Every run logs `Using triton ReplaySSM backend.` on both workers. Each run takes about 3.5 minutes. pre-commit is clean on the changed files.

The other skips in the mirror are the CUDA/SM100-only files (`test_norm_mxfp8.py`, `test_dense_gemm1_mxfp8.py`, `test_qkv_index_fused_epilogue.py`), which test NVIDIA-path CuTe DSL / FlashInfer kernels.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Support --log-level and --logging-config
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`--log-level`, `--logging-config` (including its dotted `--logging-config.*` forms) and the deprecated `--log-config-file` all default to `argparse.SUPPRESS`, so `get_non_default_args()` never sees them, and `RustFrontendProcessManager` builds the Rust frontend's `--args-json` from the non-default args. None of them reach the Rust frontend, and `vllm-rs serve` does not declare them. This PR makes the Rust frontend's logs follow the resolved level, and fails startup on the JSON formatter, which Rust does not implement yet.

## Claims

- `vllm serve --log-level DEBUG` (or `--logging-config.log_level DEBUG`) with `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1` now sets the Rust frontend's log level too, where it stayed at the `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL` default.
- `vllm-rs serve` accepts `--log-level` and `--logging-config` (plain JSON or dotted forms), with Python's precedence: `--log-level`, then `--logging-config.log_level`, then `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL`, then `INFO`. It forwards one `--logging-config` carrying the resolved level to the managed engine.
- `--logging-config.formatter json` fails startup instead of being silently ignored by the Rust frontend.
- `configure_logging` and `pylogging_config_file` configure Python logging only: Rust passes them through to the engine, and the Python launcher warns that they do not apply to the Rust frontend's logs.

## Validation

Based on `b2094acc88`.

```bash
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check                    # clean
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                                           # clean
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans # clean
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings  # clean
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2587 tests run: 2587 passed, 13 skipped
pytest tests/entrypoints/launchers/api_server/test_api_server_process_manager.py -k rust_frontend
# 10 passed, 8 deselected
```

- `vllm-cmd` CLI tests: level names in any case with Python's `WARN`/`FATAL` aliases, invalid names failing; precedence in both orders (`serve_resolves_log_level_like_python`); forwarding one config with the resolved level and the Python-only fields as given, an explicit `null` included (`serve_args_forward_log_level_to_managed_engine`, `serve_forwards_logging_config_to_managed_engine`); the JSON formatter failing in plain and dotted form (`serve_rejects_unimplemented_logging_config`); `--args-json` resolution, with the formatter error naming its field path (`frontend_args_json_resolves_logging_config`).
- `vllm-tracing`: NOTSET maps to WARN.
- `test_rust_frontend_receives_resolved_logging_config` (launcher, mocked `Popen`): six argument sets, asserting `logging_config` in `--args-json` and whether the launcher warns.

Live, `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` with `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`, one chat request each, counting Rust frontend log lines by level (measured on an earlier revision that passed the level through the child's env; the tracing filter is the same):

| Arguments | Startup | Rust DEBUG | Rust INFO |
|---|---|---|---|
| none | healthy | 0 | 16 |
| `--log-level DEBUG` | healthy | 10 | 16 |
| `--logging-config.log_level ERROR` | healthy | 0 | 0 |
| `--logging-config.formatter json` | fails | | |

## Details

**Python launcher** (`vllm/v1/utils.py`): `cli/main.py` already merges the three arguments into `args.logging_config` (`configure_logging_from_args`), so `RustFrontendProcessManager` sends its resolved `log_level` and `formatter` as `logging_config` in `--args-json`. It also owns the warning about `configure_logging` and `pylogging_config_file`, since their defaults come from env vars (`VLLM_CONFIGURE_LOGGING`, `VLLM_LOGGING_CONFIG_PATH`) that only Python reads.

**One level type** (`vllm_tracing::LogLevel`): Python's level names, parsed case-insensitively with the `WARN` and `FATAL` aliases, used for every source (`--log-level`, `--logging-config.log_level`, `--args-json`, `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL`). `init_tracing(process_label, log_level)` takes it, and `RUST_LOG` still refines it per target. NOTSET maps to WARN, where it mapped to TRACE before: Python's `vllm` logger at NOTSET defers to the root logger, which is at WARNING.

**`--logging-config`** (`cli/logging.rs`) types only the fields the Rust frontend's logs honor: `log_level`, and `formatter`, whose `LogFormatter` has only `Text` for now, so `json` fails deserialization on both `vllm-rs serve` and `--args-json`. The other keys are kept as a JSON map and forwarded as given; the engine's `LoggingConfig` forbids unknown fields, so it validates them. The JSON formatter for the Rust frontend's own logs is a separate follow-up.

**`vllm-rs serve`** consumes `--log-level` and `--logging-config` and forwards one `--logging-config` with the level it resolved. With no logging argument, nothing is forwarded and the engine reads the env vars itself. Dotted forms are merged into `--logging-config <JSON>` by vllm-project/vllm#65370. The global subscriber is installed after parsing, so parse-time warnings (no-op arguments) are emitted at the env level through a thread-local default subscriber.

**Divergence from Python.** A plain `--logging-config` given together with dotted forms fails startup on `vllm-rs serve` (clap rejects the repeated argument). Python silently drops the plain one there: `FlexibleArgumentParser` merges only the dotted forms, appends their merge as a second `--logging-config`, and argparse keeps the last.

**Left as is:** Rust logs to stderr while Python's default handler writes to stdout.

**Size.** About 220 added production lines, mostly the level type and its parsing in `vllm_tracing` and the CLI wiring; the rest is tests.

**Not a duplicate.** No open upstream PR carries the logging arguments to the Rust frontend.

**AI assistance.** This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). The human submitter reviewed every changed line and the validation results.

commits.pr_title: [Frontend] Default --enable-scale-out to VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Default `--enable-scale-out` to `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE` in the Python and Rust frontends, so RL setups that already run with dev mode need one switch instead of two. Follow-up to #61042.

## Claims

- `--enable-scale-out` defaults to `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE`, mirroring `--log-error-stack`. `--disable-scale-out` (Python) / `--enable-scale-out false` (Rust CLI) still opts out explicitly.
- Without dev mode and without the flag, behavior is unchanged.
- Docs describe how dev mode affects the default.

## Validation

```bash
pytest -q tests/entrypoints/scale_out/test_factories.py
# 26 passed

cd rust
cargo test -p vllm-cmd -- enable_scale_out log_error_stack
# 2 passed
cargo test -p vllm-server --lib scale_out
# 4 passed
cargo fmt --all -- --check
# clean
```

New tests:
- `test_enable_scale_out_defaults_to_server_dev_mode` (Python): parses `vllm serve` args in a subprocess with `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=0/1`, with and without `--disable-scale-out`. A subprocess is needed because the default is read from `envs` at import time, like `log_error_stack`.
- `enable_scale_out_defaults_to_server_dev_mode` (Rust): same matrix through the clap path and through the `--args-json` + env fallback path that Python uses to launch the Rust frontend (Python omits the flag from `--args-json` when it equals the parser default).

Not run: an end-to-end `vllm serve` with a model.

## Details

- RL needs `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE` for the RL routes in `vllm/entrypoints/rl` (registered under dev mode) and `--enable-scale-out` for `/inference/v1/generate` and `/derender`. Defaulting the flag to dev mode removes the second switch, using the same "flag defaults to dev mode" pattern as `log_error_stack`.
- Scope: this PR only changes the default. What disabled scale-out routes return (currently 403 from #61042, vs. unregistered/404 as raised in its review) is left for a separate change.
- Scale-out is not folded into dev mode entirely: render/generate are also production disaggregated-serving routes, and requiring dev mode for them would also expose routes such as `/sleep`. For the same reason the 403 hint still only points at `--enable-scale-out`.
- This is a stopgap for RL. The proper fix is to expose endpoints by role (RFC #56993, or a dedicated RL entrypoint that brings generate/derender and the weight-update routes without dev mode).

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Return routed experts on non-streaming chat and completions
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With `--enable-return-routed-experts`, the Python frontend returns the request's routed-expert rows (base64 `.npy`) on non-streaming `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/completions` choices and honors `routed_experts_prompt_start` there; the Rust frontend returns them only on `/inference/v1/generate` (vllm-project/vllm#61949). This PR brings them to the OpenAI routes, including requests the frontend ends on a stop string. It takes over closed vllm-project/vllm#63481 by Ronald1995 (credited as co-author), reimplemented on current `main`.

## Claims

| Case | Before | After (matches Python) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| non-streaming chat/completions, flag on | `routed_experts: null` | base64 `.npy` of all rows |
| ... ended by a stop string mid-output | `null` | rows up to the kept tokens |
| `routed_experts_prompt_start: N` on chat/completions | silently dropped | forwarded; out of range is a 400 |
| `/inference/v1/generate` (stream and non-stream) | rows on the final chunk | unchanged |

Streaming chat and completions stay without rows, like Python.

## Validation

`openai_non_stream_returns_routed_experts_cut_at_stop_string` (chat and completions): the mock engine sends one row per token over three outputs, the stop string ends the request locally inside the last output, and the choice's `.npy` holds exactly the kept rows; it also asserts that `routed_experts_prompt_start: 1` reaches the engine. On `main` the field is `null`; without the stop-string cut the shape is `(5, 1, 2)`; without the completions forwarding the engine sees `0`. Unit tests cover the row operations (join, cut across chunks, shape mismatch, unresolved data) and per-output rows through generate streaming and `stream_interval` merging.

Rust CI set (`.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh`) on this branch:

```bash
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check                    # clean
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                                           # clean
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans # clean
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings  # clean
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2562 tests run: 2562 passed, 13 skipped
```

Not covered: a live MoE run (`tests/entrypoints/rl/return_routed_experts/test_openai_api.py` needs Model Runner V2 and `TitanML/tiny-mixtral`); it can join the Rust frontend CI steps after this lands.

## Details

**Why the rows change shape.** `vllm-llm` joined the rows only on an engine-finished output, but `vllm-text` ends a stop-string request locally and drops the engine stream first, so such a request had no rows at all. Python keeps the rows received so far, cuts those of tokens past the stop (`OutputProcessor._trim_surplus_tokens`), and concatenates on finish. Here `GenerateOutput` now carries the rows the engine sent with that output; each consumer that keeps outputs (generate streaming, generate collect, text decoding) appends them and joins once at the end, and text decoding drops the rows of the cut tokens next to its token, logprob and sampling-mask truncation. The joined rows travel with the other terminal metadata to the non-streaming choices.

**Reusable rows.** The rows are kept in `AuxOutputRows`, whose operations are generic NumPy-style row operations on `WireNdArray` (`truncate_rows`, `concat_rows`, failing with a typed `ArrayRowsError`). The next token-aligned auxiliary output, `indexer_topk` in open vllm-project/vllm#49555, needs the same append, stop-string cut and join, and can add one more `AuxOutputRows` field. This is the inline delivery mode; the store-based delivery proposed in vllm-project/vllm#64380 and vllm-project/vllm#64383 is orthogonal to it.

**Commits.** (1) move `npy_base64` into `server/src/utils` so the OpenAI routes can encode rows; (2) the change itself; (3) remove the docs line saying the Rust HTTP frontend never returns `routed_experts`.

**Not a duplicate.** Supersedes closed vllm-project/vllm#63481; no other open PR returns routed experts from the Rust OpenAI routes.

**AI assistance.** This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). The human submitter reviewed every changed line and the validation results.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Export SimpleCPUOffload KV connector metrics
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` reports five Prometheus families from its scheduler (vllm-project/vllm#57251, `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/metrics.py`), which the Python frontend exports. The Rust frontend decodes only NIXL, Mooncake and UMBP connector payloads, so a SimpleCPUOffload payload falls into the opaque `Multi`/`Other` path and none of the families appear on `/metrics`. This PR adds a typed decoder and records the five families, as was done for the Mooncake transfer (vllm-project/vllm#63317) and UMBP (vllm-project/vllm#64512) connectors. The first commit is Ao Shen's (aoshen02), kept with his authorship.

## Claims

The Rust frontend exports these families when the connector is active, as a sole connector or as a `MultiConnector` child:

| Metric | Type | Extra labels |
|---|---|---|
| `vllm:simple_kv_offload_save_outcomes_total` | counter | `outcome` |
| `vllm:simple_kv_offload_load_blocks_total` | counter | |
| `vllm:simple_kv_offload_used_blocks` | gauge | |
| `vllm:simple_kv_offload_pending_store_blocks` | gauge | |
| `vllm:simple_kv_offload_info` | gauge (always 1) | `backend`, `page_cache`, `lazy_offload`, `capacity_blocks` |

Deployments without the connector show no series, as in Python.

## Validation

Rust CI set (`.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh`) on this branch, based on `3cd3a7ad1c`:

```bash
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check                    # clean
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                                           # clean
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans # clean
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings  # clean
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2581 tests run: 2581 passed, 13 skipped
```

The first commit on its own also passes clippy with `-D warnings` and the `vllm-engine-core-client` and `vllm-metrics` tests.

- `metrics::tests::simple_cpu_offload_stats_are_recorded_into_simple_kv_offload_metrics`: no series before the connector reports; one flat interval and one `MultiConnector` child interval add up the counters and keep the latest gauges (snapshot of the rendered series). Fails with the `MultiConnector` child recording removed.
- `python_msgpack_fixtures_match_rust_encoding_and_record_nixl_metrics`: a payload encoded with `msgspec` as Python does (tuple keys) decodes as `SimpleCpuOffload`; the `MultiConnector` fixture carries a SimpleCPUOffload child that reaches `/metrics`; an unknown metric in the payload is ignored (fails with `deny_unknown_fields`); and an OffloadingConnector `types`/`data` payload does not decode as SimpleCPUOffload (fails with `used_blocks` made optional).

## Details

**Payload.** The engine sends the families in `SchedulerStats.kv_connector_stats` as `{"types": {name: "counter" | "gauge"}, "data": {name: {label-value tuple: value}}}`, flat or as the `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` child of a `MultiConnector` payload.

**Second commit: alignment with the other connector decoders on `main`.**

- Unknown fields are ignored, as `KvConnectorStats` documents for the typed payloads; strict decoding would drop this connector's stats, and inside a `MultiConnector` its siblings' too, as soon as Python adds a metric. The `used_blocks` gauge, which `SimpleCPUOffloadScheduler.get_stats` sets every interval, is the required field that keeps the flat payload apart from other connectors' `types`/`data` payloads (OffloadingConnector, `vllm:kv_offload_*`).
- Only `data` is read: each metric's type is fixed by its name, so there is no `types` cross-check.
- Values are `u64` (block counts and the constant 1 of the info gauge, as the producer emits them), recorded into the existing `U64Counter`/`U64Gauge`.
- Rust naming (`SimpleCpuOffload*`); series are created when the connector first reports (`Family`, like the Mooncake store and UMBP families).
- No Rust-specific docs section: `docs/usage/metrics.md` already documents these metrics from `metrics.py`.

**Layering.** The wire type lives with the other connector payloads in `engine-core-client/src/protocol/stats.rs` (`KvConnectorStats::SimpleCpuOffload`, `MultiConnectorStats::simple_cpu_offload`), the families in `vllm-metrics` next to the Mooncake and UMBP ones, and the recording in `SchedulerStatsRecorder`, the consumer of `SchedulerStats.kv_connector_stats`.

**Not a duplicate.** Based on Ao Shen's fork-only aoshen02/vllm#181; no open upstream PR exports these families from the Rust frontend.

**AI assistance.** This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). The human submitter reviewed every changed line and the validation results.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Join text parts in the renderer for DeepSeek V3.2 and /v1/responses
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

A message whose `content` is a list of text parts renders differently on the two frontends in two places: the Rust DeepSeek V3.2 renderer concatenates the parts, and the Rust `/v1/responses` converter glues them together before any renderer sees them. This PR moves the join into the renderer, as on the Chat Completions path for HF templates (vllm-project/vllm#63974, vllm-project/vllm#65623). Issue vllm-project/vllm#63917, item 1, names the V3.2 renderer.

## Claims

| Case | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DeepSeek V3.2, content `["Part one. ", "Part two."]` (any role) | `Part one. Part two.` | `Part one. \nPart two.`, empty parts dropped (matches Python) |
| `/v1/responses` `function_call_output` with `["Sunny", "25C"]` | `Sunny25C` | each renderer's join, e.g. `Sunny\n25C` for HF templates (matches Python) |
| `/v1/responses` assistant `message` item with two `output_text` parts | one glued text block | one text block per part, as Chat Completions lowers the same message |

## Validation

Rust CI set (`.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh`) on this branch, based on `3cd3a7ad1c`:

```bash
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check                    # clean
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                                           # clean
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans # clean
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings  # clean
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2582 tests run: 2582 passed, 13 skipped
```

- `text_parts_are_joined_with_newlines_like_python` (V3.2) renders system (with an empty part), user, assistant (two text blocks plus a tool call), tool and a final user message from parts, and matches Python's prompt byte for byte (Python's `parse_chat_messages(content_format="string")` plus `encode_messages(thinking_mode="chat")` on `main`). With the renderer change reverted it fails (`Sys one.Sys two.<｜User｜>Part one. Part two.…`).
- `text_parts_reach_the_renderer_as_parts` (Responses converter) converts user, two-part assistant, `function_call` and two-part `function_call_output` items. On `main` it fails with `Text { text: "Let me check.One moment." }` and `ToolResponse { content: Text("Sunny25C") }`.
- Existing V3.2 tests and fixtures (single-string content) are unchanged, including the multimodal rejection.

No server-level Python test sends list content to the V3.2 renderer or to `/v1/responses`.

## Details

**DeepSeek V3.2 (first commit).** Python's `DeepseekV32Renderer` parses messages with `content_format="string"` (`vllm/renderers/deepseek_v32.py`), so `parse_chat_message_content_parts` drops empty text parts and joins the rest with `"\n"` for every role before `encode_messages` runs. Rust's `write_chat_content` and `write_assistant_text` (`rust/src/chat/src/renderer/deepseek_v32/encoding.rs`) concatenated them, giving a different prompt and token count for the same request. The official V3.2 encoder takes string content only and defines no join, so the frontend's parse is the reference; the same `"\n"` join is what both frontends use for HF string-format templates. The join lives in the V3.2 renderer (one local `write_text_parts`); the shared `ChatContent::try_flatten_to_text` and assistant text helpers stay plain concatenations, since the Harmony renderer and output aggregation use them.

The other renderers issue vllm-project/vllm#63917 lists need no change: Inkling already matches Python (each text part is its own `<|content_text|>` block, as in the official template), and the Kimi K3 renderer follows the official `encoding_k3.py`, which concatenates text parts; Python reaches that encoder only after its generic string parse has joined them, so its output follows from that pre-parse rather than from the K3 format.

**`/v1/responses` (second commit).** Python passes a list `function_call_output` to the chat parser as a tool message's `content` (`_construct_message_from_response_item`, `vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/utils.py`), so it is joined like a chat tool message (vllm-project/vllm#39899). The Rust converter now keeps the parts: `function_call_output` becomes a parts tool response, and each assistant part becomes its own text block, as `convert_assistant_text_blocks` does for Chat Completions. Each renderer then applies its own join (`"\n"` for HF templates, a blank line for DeepSeek V4/V4.1, the official encoders' rules for Kimi K3 and Inkling). `ResponseMessageContent::flatten_text` becomes `into_text_content` (same non-text rejection), and assistant items are lowered in one step by `assistant_text_blocks` (text, output text and refusal parts; anything else is a 400 naming the part type).

**Intentional difference from Python.** For an assistant `message` item, Python keeps only `content[0]` and silently drops the other parts; this PR keeps every part, so `/v1/responses` and Chat Completions render the same history the same way.

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR changes the V3.2 text-part join or the Responses content lowering in the Rust frontend.

**AI assistance.** This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). The human submitter reviewed every changed line and the validation results.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Accept `spaces_between_special_tokens` as a no-op
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`spaces_between_special_tokens` (default `true`) is a vLLM sampling option on chat completions, completions and Responses. The Rust frontend rejects `false` with a 400 on all three routes. For the tokenizers it serves, its incremental detokenizer already produces what `false` asks for (adjacent added tokens with no inserted separator), so this PR accepts the field as a documented no-op.

## Claims

- `spaces_between_special_tokens: false` no longer returns a 400 on `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/completions` and `/v1/responses`; `true` keeps working.
- Detokenized output is unchanged, and it matches Python's `false` output on the served tokenizers we measured (below), without Python's raw-content artifacts on Gemma 2/3.

## Validation

Rust CI set (`.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh`) on this branch, based on `3cd3a7ad1c`:

```bash
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check                    # clean
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                                           # clean
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans # clean
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings  # clean
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2583 tests run: 2583 passed, 13 skipped
```

Each validator now accepts `false`; with the three 400 checks restored, the three new validator tests fail.

**Parity scan.** Python's `FastIncrementalDetokenizer` (`vllm/v1/engine/detokenizer.py`, `skip_special_tokens=false`) against Rust's `HuggingFaceTokenizer` plus `create_decode_stream`, on every cached `tokenizer.json` checkpoint (304 fast tokenizers, loaded through vLLM's `get_tokenizer`; transformers 5.22.0, tokenizers 0.23.3), over text plus 80 consecutive added tokens:

- 298 tokenizers give Python identical text for `true` and `false`; the other 4 are three WordPiece encoders (`bert-base-uncased`, `BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5`, `cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2`; pooling-only, not served by the Rust frontend) and `deepseek-ai/deepseek-moe-16b-base`, whose ByteLevel decoder garbles some added tokens.
- Rust's output equals Python's `false` output on 293 of them; the WordPiece encoders and deepseek-moe match Python's `true`, and `AIDC-AI/Ovis2.5-2B` differs from Python for both values (an unrelated tokenizer-loading difference).

## Details

**What `false` does in Python.** When special tokens are kept, the fast detokenizer emits an added token that directly follows another added token as its raw content instead of the `DecodeStream` text. The option changes the text only when two added tokens are adjacent and the decoder's output differs from the raw content.

**Why not port it.** Where `false` does change served output, Python's behavior is wrong rather than a target. In Gemma 2 and 3 tokenizers, `\n` and runs of spaces are added tokens (`138: "▁▁"`, `139: "▁▁▁"`, …) whose raw content is the Metaspace `▁`. With `google/gemma-3-1b-it`, the tokens of `"def f():\n        return 1"` detokenize in Python to `def f():\n        return 1` with `true` but to `def f():\n▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁return 1` with `false`, because the raw-content substitution skips the decoder's `▁` → space replacement; Rust emits `def f():\n        return 1`. A decoder implementation (an added-token join in `DecodeStream`, about 40 production lines) matched Python on the sampled tokenizers but changed output only for the WordPiece encoders, the deepseek-moe case and Gemma 2/3, where it reproduced the corruption.

**Layering.** The value would only steer the incremental detokenizer in `vllm-tokenizer`, which already produces `false`'s output, so the change is at the DTO validation boundary that held the 400: the checks are dropped and the field is documented as a no-op on the request DTOs.

**Left as is.** With the default `true`, Python's slow tokenizers (tiktoken, Mistral) join added tokens with a space, while Rust's tiktoken and Tekken backends never do; Python's Kimi K3 and `response_template` parsers force `false` to avoid exactly that spacing. gRPC has no such field.

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR changes this option in the Rust frontend.

**AI assistance.** This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). The human submitter reviewed every changed line and the validation results.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Support tool_reference content parts
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Tool search clients answer a tool search call with a tool result that names the tools found, as vLLM's `tool_reference` content parts (vllm-project/vllm#40190):

```json
{"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "call_1", "content": [{"type": "tool_reference", "name": "get_weather"}]}
```

The Python frontend accepts the part and hands it to the renderer. The Rust frontend does not know the part type, so every such request fails with a 400 at deserialization, although `defer_loading` on tools (the other half of tool search) is already supported. This PR accepts the part and renders it per model.

## Claims

| Renderer | After this PR |
| --- | --- |
| HF, `openai` content format | `{"type": "tool_reference", "name": ...}` reaches the template (matches Python) |
| HF, `string` content format | the tool name in the part's place, joined with `"\n"` (matches Python) |
| GLM-5.3 (`glm5_next`) | the referenced tool's definition is expanded, as the checkpoint template does (matches Python) |
| DeepSeek V4 | the tool name; every tool listed up front, deferred ones included (deepseek-recipe) |
| DeepSeek V4.1 | the tool name; deferred tools listed only once referenced, in an `### Updated Tool Schemas` system turn (deepseek-recipe) |
| DeepSeek V3.2, Kimi K3, Inkling, Harmony | 400 "`tool_reference` content parts are not supported by this chat renderer" |

A reference to a tool that is neither a request-level nor a message-scoped tool is a 400 on every renderer.

## Validation

Rust CI set (`.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh`) on this branch, based on `3cd3a7ad1c`:

```bash
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check                    # clean
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                                           # clean
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans # clean
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings  # clean
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2587 tests run: 2587 passed, 13 skipped
```

- `prepare_chat_request_maps_tool_reference_parts`: the JSON part deserializes and lowers onto the tool message (a 400 on `main`); a reference to an unknown tool is a 400. `resolved_tool_context_rejects_unknown_tool_references`: request-level and message-scoped tools both resolve references.
- `assistant_and_tool_content_parts_reach_templates` (HF): a tool message with a text and a tool-reference part renders as `"x\nget_weather"` (`string`) and as the structured list (`openai`).
- `tool_references_expand_like_existing_hf_renderer` (GLM-5.3): with the referenced tool deferred, native renders equal HF renders of both checkpoint templates in `openai` and `auto` content format and contain the expanded definition.
- `tool_references_list_deferred_tools_like_deepseek_recipe` (V4.1) and `tool_references_render_as_tool_names_like_deepseek_recipe` (V4): the expected prompts are deepseek-recipe's own render of the equivalent Messages request (a tool-search tool, two deferred tools, a result referencing both, then user text), byte for byte. `tool_references_keep_order_and_duplicates` and `rejects_requests_whose_tools_are_all_deferred` (V4.1) are checked against recipe's output for the same requests. With the first commit's renderer, the four DeepSeek tests fail.

No server-level Python test sends a chat `tool_reference` part (the render test in `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/render/test_render.py` goes through `/v1/messages/render`, which the Rust frontend does not serve).

## Details

**Commits.** (1) The part end to end: `ContentPart::ToolReference { name }` in the chat DTO, lowered to `ChatContentPart::ToolReference { name }` in `vllm-chat`, and handled in each renderer's own exhaustive `match`, so no shared flattening helper starts treating it as text. Assistant messages keep accepting only text and refusal parts. (2) The shared unknown-reference check and the DeepSeek V4/V4.1 rendering.

**Shared check.** `ResolvedToolContext::new` (chat, Responses and `/tokenize` alike) rejects a reference that names no request-level or message-scoped tool, as deepseek-recipe does, so renderers can look the tool up with the new `ChatRequest::tool(name)`. The full tool set is authoritative: with `--exclude-tools-when-tool-choice-none` and `tool_choice: none`, the request-level tools leave the prompt after this check.

**DeepSeek V4/V4.1.** These follow deepseek-recipe (`935817c`, its Messages conversion and the `dsv4.rs`/`dsv41.rs` encoders), the reference implementation for these models. On V4.1, after a user turn whose tool results reference tools, the renderer writes `<｜System｜>\n\n### Updated Tool Schemas\n\n` and the referenced tools' schemas, one per line, in reference order and with duplicates, exactly as recipe's mid-conversation system message; a request whose tools are all deferred is a 400, as in recipe. A name containing the image placeholder is rejected like message text.

**Differences from Python.**

- DeepSeek V4.1: Python (vllm-project/vllm#64971) lists every tool, deferred ones included, and writes only the name. Following deepseek-recipe keeps the prompt prefix stable and saves the deferred schemas' tokens.
- DeepSeek V4: Python's encoder rejects the part; this PR writes the name, as deepseek-recipe does.
- An unknown reference is a 400; Python passes it on (GLM-5.3's template renders an empty `<tools></tools>`).
- Kimi K3, DeepSeek V3.2 and Harmony: Python's result there falls out of generic flattening (the name, or `""` on Harmony) rather than a choice for these encoders, and nothing shows the bare name is what these models expect, so the Rust frontend rejects the part explicitly. Python's Inkling encoder rejects it too.
- A `tool_reference` without `name` fails deserialization; Python keeps `{"name": None}` or drops the part.

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR adds `tool_reference` parts to the Rust frontend.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Export vllm:request_render_duration_seconds
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

vllm-project/vllm#60213 added `vllm:request_render_duration_seconds` to the Python frontend (`vllm/renderers/metrics.py`): a histogram of the time `OnlineRenderer` spends turning a request into engine inputs, labeled `model_name` and `request_type` (`chat` or `completion`), observed only when rendering succeeds. The Rust frontend has no such family, so `/metrics` under `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1` lacks it and dashboards built on it go blank. This PR exports it from the Rust chat and text facades.

## Claims

- `vllm:request_render_duration_seconds` is registered with Python's name, help text, label names and buckets (0.1 ms to 10 s).
- Chat completions and `/v1/responses` record `request_type="chat"`; completions and gRPC `Generate`/`GenerateStream` record `request_type="completion"`; failed renders record nothing, like Python.
- `model_name` is the primary served model name, as for every other frontend metric.

## Validation

Rust CI set (`.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh`) on this branch, based on `3cd3a7ad1c`:

```bash
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check                    # clean
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                                           # clean
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans # clean
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings  # clean
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2581 tests run: 2581 passed, 13 skipped
```

- `vllm-metrics` `request_render_duration_matches_python_exposition` snapshots the exposition: name, help text, labels and all 16 buckets (the cases of Python's `tests/renderers/test_metrics.py`, except lazy registration, see below).
- `vllm-server` `request_metrics_use_served_model_name_label` sends a chat request whose render fails (400), then one chat, one completions and one Responses request for a served-name alias against the mock engine, and checks two `chat` and one `completion` observations under the primary served name. With the observations removed it fails (`chat: left 0.0, right 2.0`); without the served name set on the facade the label falls back to the backend model ID and it fails too.
- `vllm-server` `grpc::tests::unary_generate_returns_collected_text` checks one `completion` observation for a gRPC text prompt; it fails if `generate` prepares on its own instead of going through `generate_n`.

## Details

**Where it is recorded.** The metric measures the renderer, so the facades that render record it, like Python's `OnlineRenderer`:

- `vllm-chat`: `ChatLlm::chat_n` times `ChatRequestProcessor::prepare` (template rendering, multimodal preprocessing, tokenization, output-parser initialization) and records `chat`.
- `vllm-text`: `TextLlm::generate_n` times `TextRequestProcessor::prepare` (tokenization, truncation, lowering) and records `completion`. `TextLlm::generate` now goes through `generate_n` (the unused `generate_prepared` is removed), so gRPC records it too. The chat path submits through `generate_prepared_n`, so a chat request is counted once. `generate_raw`, the token-in-token-out path of `/inference/v1/generate`, records nothing, like Python.

The families live in a new `renderer` module of `vllm-metrics` (`METRICS.renderer`), with `request_type` as a closed enum, `RenderRequestType::{Chat, Completion}`. Like Python's, the buckets are fixed and not part of `--custom-histogram-buckets`. `vllm-chat` and `vllm-text` take a dependency on the leaf `vllm-metrics` crate, as `vllm-llm` and `vllm-engine-core-client` do. The HTTP handlers are unchanged.

**Label.** `TextLlm` carries the frontend's primary served name (`with_served_model_name` and `served_model_name`, also on `ChatLlm`; the backend model ID by default), which `build_state` sets to the same name as every other frontend metric label. It is a frontend setting, so it stays off `LlmInfo`, which describes the engine: with a provided `Llm` (a router in front of remote workers) the engine's name and the frontend's `--served-model-name` can differ.

**Differences from Python.**

- `/v1/responses` records `chat`: it renders through `ChatLlm::chat_n` like chat completions. Python's `render_responses` records nothing.
- gRPC `Generate` records `completion`: it tokenizes through the same `TextLlm` path. Python's gRPC servicer bypasses `OnlineRenderer`.
- The span starts at the facade, so the HTTP DTO lowering is not included; Python's starts at the top of `render_chat`/`render_completion`. The chat span includes Rust's output-parser and output-grammar setup, which belong to `prepare`.
- `/tokenize` and `/inference/v1/generate` do not record it. Python records it on `/tokenize` only for gpt-oss chat requests, which go through `render_chat`.
- `vllm-rs render` serves no `/metrics`, so the render server does not export it (a separate gap).
- Python registers the family lazily, so its `# HELP` line appears only after the first render; Rust registers it at startup like the other families, with no series until the first request.

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR adds this metric to the Rust frontend.

**AI assistance.** This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). The human submitter reviewed every changed line and the validation results.

commits.pr_title: [Model][Qwen4Exp] Run routed experts on DeepGEMM MegaMoE (MXFP8 or MXFP4)
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

> [!NOTE]
> This description was edited by Claude (an AI assistant) with authorization from Thien Tran (gau-nernst). The previous version is in the edit history.


## Overview

Runs Qwen4Exp (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) routed experts on the DeepGEMM MegaMoE backend (`--kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}'`, built on `DeepGemmMegaMoEExperts` from #61538). Expert parallelism is required.

The routed experts load in the checkpoint's format when MegaMoE can run it, and are requantized otherwise:

| Checkpoint experts | Default MegaMoE format | Forced with `--quantization` / `--quantization-config` |
|---|---|---|
| BF16 (official `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next`, fused `gate_up_proj` / `down_proj`) | BF16, loaded as stored | `mxfp8` or `mxfp4` |
| 128x128 block FP8 (official `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8`) | MXFP8, requantized with a warning | `mxfp8` or `mxfp4` |
| MXFP8 (ModelOpt) | MXFP8, loaded as stored | `mxfp4` |
| MXFP4 (Quark) | MXFP4, loaded as stored | `mxfp8` |

## Claims

- Qwen4Exp serves on `deep_gemm_mega_moe` with DP + EP on Blackwell, from the official BF16 and FP8 checkpoints. MXFP8 and MXFP4 checkpoints load directly; no public one exists yet, so that path is covered by unit tests only (format detection is tested for ModelOpt MXFP8; Quark MXFP4 goes through vLLM's existing Quark config lookup).
- Accuracy matches the default MoE backend on GSM8K (table below). MXFP8 and MXFP4 MegaMoE also pass non-inferiority against stock FP8 on AIME25, AIME26, GPQA-Diamond and MMMU-Pro.
- B300, FP8 checkpoint, vs the default MoE backend on the same commit:
  - TP1 prefill throughput: +12-13% (MXFP8), +15-16% (MXFP4).
  - DEP4 decode output throughput: +13-17% (MXFP8), +23-25% (MXFP4); mean TPOT -10-13% / -18-20%.
- Works with layerwise reload and chunked weight updates that deliver every expert shard (see Limitations).

## Validation

### Unit tests

`pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_mega_moe.py`: 10 passed on GB200. They run in the existing `qwen4-exp-hc-kernels-b200` Buildkite step. The tests cover:
- format selection from the checkpoint and the online quantization config, including `ignore`, `targets` and forced MXFP8/MXFP4;
- loading per-expert block-FP8, MXFP8 and MXFP4 tensors and the official checkpoint's fused BF16 tensors into the kernel layout on one EP rank of two, bitwise equal to the generic `DeepGemmMegaMoEExperts.weight_loader` fed tensors requantized with DeepGEMM's own casts;
- weight and scale arriving in separate `load_weights` calls, and the post-load error on an incomplete pair (requantized formats);
- layerwise reload replacing the experts in the original storage.

The MegaMoE kernels themselves are covered by `tests/kernels/moe/test_deep_gemm_mega_moe.py`. CI does not run `Qwen4ExpMegaMoeBlock`'s forward or the decoder's backend selection; the GSM8K runs below cover them end to end.

### GSM8K

4x GB200 node, DP4 + EP, MTP3 speculative decoding, 5-shot, greedy, thinking off, full test set (1319 questions), one run per arm:

| Checkpoint | MoE backend | Experts | flexible / strict |
|---|---|---|---|
| BF16 | default | BF16 | 96.82 / 96.82 |
| BF16 | MegaMoE | BF16, as stored | 96.74 / 96.82 |
| FP8 | default | block FP8 | 97.19 / 97.27 |
| FP8 | MegaMoE | MXFP8, requantized | 96.66 / 96.74 |

Four runs of the FP8 MegaMoE arm on different revisions of this branch scored 96.59-96.89 flexible. The requantized weights are identical across those revisions, so this range is run-to-run noise.

### Reasoning evals and throughput (FP8 checkpoint, B300)

These were measured on an earlier revision of this PR. The FP8 -> MXFP8/MXFP4 requantization is numerically unchanged since then: same DeepGEMM casts, applied row by row.

Reasoning evals with thinking on, `temperature=1.0, top_p=0.95, top_k=20`, `max_tokens=98304`, MTP3. Stock FP8 is TP4 + EP on the default MoE backend; MegaMoE is DP4 + EP. Rule: paired difference vs stock with a bootstrap 95% CI; non-inferior if the lower bound is >= -2 pt (AIME) or -1 pt (GPQA-D, MMMU-Pro).

| Benchmark | Stock FP8 | MegaMoE MXFP8 | Δ vs stock [95% CI] | MegaMoE MXFP4 | Δ vs stock [95% CI] |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AIME25 | 99.69 | 99.69 | +0.00 [-0.52, +0.52] | 99.32 | -0.36 [-1.04, +0.16] |
| AIME26 | 97.19 | 97.50 | +0.31 [-0.52, +1.15] | 96.77 | -0.42 [-1.88, +0.73] |
| GPQA-Diamond | 90.81 | 91.26 | +0.44 [-0.19, +1.10] | 90.74 | -0.08 [-0.84, +0.66] |
| MMMU-Pro (flexible) | 76.82 | 77.02 | +0.20 [-0.52, +0.92] | 76.73 | -0.09 [-0.70, +0.51] |

`vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --ignore-eos`, `--max-num-seqs 256 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --no-enable-prefix-caching`, no speculative decoding; each point run twice (runs differed by <= 3%).

| Prefill, TP1, 1 output token | Stock tok/s | MXFP8 | MXFP4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8192 x 256 prompts, concurrency 64 | 45,188 | 51,009 (+12.9%) | 52,441 (+16.1%) |
| 32768 x 64 prompts, concurrency 16 | 43,252 | 48,633 (+12.4%) | 49,865 (+15.3%) |

| Decode, DP4 + EP, 2048 in / 1024 out | Stock out tok/s | MXFP8 | MXFP4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| concurrency 128 | 8,348 | 9,456 (+13.3%) | 10,447 (+25.1%) |
| concurrency 256 | 12,453 | 14,045 (+12.8%) | 15,269 (+22.6%) |
| concurrency 512 | 17,268 | 20,123 (+16.5%) | 21,356 (+23.7%) |

### Weight loading

FP8 checkpoint -> MXFP8 on GB200: `Loading weights took` 48 s per rank at DP4 + EP, and 148 s at TP1. TP1 is the worst case: one rank requantizes all 512 experts of 48 layers, one expert projection at a time. Batching a projection's experts loaded in 120 s at TP1, but needed a chunking bound and a deferred flush; the simpler per-expert path was preferred.

## Details

**Format selection.** There is no new flag. `mega_moe_expert_formats` reads the checkpoint's expert format (`Fp8Config`, or `get_checkpoint_quant_keys` for ModelOpt and Quark), then applies the online quantization config per layer. `moe` or `targets` forces MXFP8 or MXFP4. Layers matched by `ignore` keep the default. Requantized layers show in the online quantization summary. The MTP drafter's config does not carry the online config, so its experts take the default format.

**Loading.** Experts in a MegaMoE format are written straight into the kernel layout through each parameter's `weight_loader`, as for DeepSeek V4, Kimi K3 and MiniMax M3. Other experts are requantized one expert projection at a time, as soon as its weight and scale have both arrived: dequantize to FP32, then DeepGEMM's `per_token_cast_to_fp8` / `per_token_cast_to_fp4` with UE8M0 scales over 1x32 groups. The results go through the same `weight_loader`, so layerwise reload (`reload_weights`, NCCL/IPC weight transfer) can buffer and replay them. A chunked update may split an expert's weight from its scale; the half pair waits for the next `load_weights` call, and `process_weights_after_loading` fails on any pair still incomplete.

**Shared expert.** Qwen4Exp gates the shared expert per token with `sigmoid(shared_expert_gate(x))`, which MegaMoE's fused shared expert cannot apply, so the shared expert stays unfused. It runs on an auxiliary stream while the router and top-k run (`maybe_execute_in_parallel`, which runs both on one stream under breakable CUDA graph capture), and joins before the MegaMoE launch, which needs every SM. `VLLM_DISABLE_SHARED_EXPERTS_STREAM` turns the overlap off.

**Other changes.** The DeepGEMM MegaMoE warmup covers Qwen4Exp blocks, and its cache key includes the routed-expert format.

**Docs.** None, as for the other DeepGEMM MegaMoE integrations (GLM-5.3-Flash, Kimi K3, MiniMax M3, Step5): the docs do not cover the `deep_gemm_mega_moe` backend for any model.

**Limitations.**
- TP > 1 is rejected (it needs sequence-parallel inputs on the HC path); use DP + EP. Non-linear `--expert-placement-strategy` is rejected.
- NVFP4 is not wired up. At Qwen4Exp's intermediate size (640, not a multiple of 256), the pinned DeepGEMM `nvfp4_mega_moe` kernel issues `ceil(640 / 256) = 3` TMA stages per L2 task while the MMA warp consumes `floor = 2`. Large launches hang and small ones return wrong output.
- Explicit activation precisions in the online config are ignored: MegaMoE fixes them per kernel (MXFP8 dispatch for MX experts, BF16 for BF16).
- Mixing MXFP8 and MXFP4 layers allocates one symmetric buffer per MMA type, about 1-2.6 GiB per GPU each for these shapes. Pooling them is a follow-up in the generic MegaMoE layer.
- EPLB plumbing comes from `DeepGemmMegaMoEExperts` but was not exercised here.
- A layerwise reload that sends a layer's weights without any of their scales writes nothing to that layer: vLLM restores its previous experts (logging `Failed to load weights`), and the unpaired tensors stay buffered. For natively loaded MXFP8/MXFP4 experts, a missing scale is caught only when no scale of that parameter arrives at all, as for the other MegaMoE models.
- Moving DeepGEMM MegaMoE behind the MoE oracle, as #63229 does for AITER MegaMoE, would let it reuse the generic online requantization. That is a cross-model refactor left for later.

---

commits.pr_title: [Doc] Fix stale attention_kernels.cu reference in paged_attention.md
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Found this while doing a structured read-through of the request lifecycle (API server → scheduler → KV cache manager → attention backends) to get oriented in the codebase. `docs/design/paged_attention.md` states in the present tense that vLLM "currently" uses a custom kernel at `csrc/attention/attention_kernels.cu`. That file no longer exists — paged attention is now implemented per-backend (e.g. `TritonAttentionImpl` in `vllm/v1/attention/backends/triton_attn.py`, or the FlashAttention backend), using block tables the scheduler's `KVCacheManager` builds. `vllm/v1/attention/ops/paged_attn.py` only has KV-cache layout helpers now (`split_kv_cache`, `write_to_paged_cache`), not the attention computation itself.

Before drafting this, I searched open and closed issues/PRs for existing coverage. #48916 already audits stale doc references across the repo, but its author explicitly left this file alone "on purpose (it has an explicit historical-document warning banner)." This PR is narrower and doesn't overlap: the doc's banner covers the step-by-step kernel walkthrough as a whole, but the specific present-tense claim about a since-deleted file is still misleading on its own, regardless of the banner. Scoped to that one paragraph — the rest of the historical walkthrough is untouched.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Report reasoning and cached tokens in chat derender usage
commits.pr_body:
## Overview `/v1/chat/completions/derender` now fills `usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens` from the reasoning parser and `usage.prompt_tokens_details` from the generate usage, in batch and stream mode, as `/v1/chat/completions` does. Fixes #64038 ## Claims - Batch and stream chat derender report `completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens` when a reasoning parser is configured. Before: `null`. - Both pass `prompt_tokens_details` through from the generate usage. Before: `null`. - Stream with `n > 1` keeps `completion_tokens_details` `null` (see Details). - 3 new tests (fail on the base commit, pass here), 2 extended; both derender test files pass in full. ## Validation CPU only. Render server on main at 39e6a1aafc (before) and on this branch (after); the generate usage is hand-built with `cached_tokens: 8`. ```bash vllm launch render Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --port 18100 --reasoning-parser qwen3 ``` ```bash python usage.py ```
usage.py ```python import json import sys import requests from transformers import AutoTokenizer from vllm.parser import ParserManager BASE = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "http://localhost:18100" M = "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B" tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(M) def post(path, body): r = requests.post(BASE + path, json=body) r.raise_for_status() return r.json() chat = {"model": M, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello"}], "max_tokens": 64} gen_req = post("/v1/chat/completions/render", chat) prompt_ids = gen_req["token_ids"] out_ids = tok.encode( "\nThe user wants a greeting.\n\n\nHello!", add_special_tokens=False ) + [tok.convert_tokens_to_ids("<|im_end|>")] gen_usage = { "prompt_tokens": len(prompt_ids), "completion_tokens": len(out_ids), "total_tokens": len(prompt_ids) + len(out_ids), "prompt_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 8}, } choice = {"index": 0, "token_ids": out_ids, "finish_reason": "stop"} batch = post("/v1/chat/completions/derender", { "model": M, "chat_request": chat, "prompt_token_ids": prompt_ids, "generate_response": {"request_id": "b", "usage": gen_usage, "choices": [choice]}, }) stream = post("/v1/chat/completions/derender", { "stream": True, "model": M, "chat_request": {**chat, "stream": True}, "prompt_token_ids": prompt_ids, "generate_chunk": {"request_id": "s", "usage": gen_usage, "choices": [choice]}, }) print("message:", json.dumps(batch["choices"][0]["message"], ensure_ascii=False)) print("derender batch usage:", json.dumps(batch["usage"])) print("derender stream usage:", json.dumps(stream["chunk"]["usage"])) parser = ParserManager.get_parser(reasoning_parser_name="qwen3", tokenizer=tok)(tok, None) print( "coupled /v1/chat/completions would report (computed with the parser, not run): " f"prompt_tokens={len(prompt_ids)}, " f"completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens={parser.count_reasoning_tokens(out_ids)}, " "prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens=8 (with --enable-prompt-tokens-details)" ) ```
Before: ```text derender batch usage: {"prompt_tokens": 0, "total_tokens": 13, "completion_tokens": 13, "prompt_tokens_details": null, "completion_tokens_details": null} derender stream usage: {"prompt_tokens": 10, "total_tokens": 23, "completion_tokens": 13, "prompt_tokens_details": null, "completion_tokens_details": null} coupled /v1/chat/completions would report (computed with the parser, not run): prompt_tokens=10, completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens=7, prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens=8 (with --enable-prompt-tokens-details) ``` After: ```text derender batch usage: {"prompt_tokens": 0, "total_tokens": 13, "completion_tokens": 13, "prompt_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 8, "created_cache_tokens": null, "multimodal_tokens": null}, "completion_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 7}} derender stream usage: {"prompt_tokens": 10, "total_tokens": 23, "completion_tokens": 13, "prompt_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 8, "created_cache_tokens": null, "multimodal_tokens": null}, "completion_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 7}} coupled /v1/chat/completions would report (computed with the parser, not run): prompt_tokens=10, completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens=7, prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens=8 (with --enable-prompt-tokens-details) ``` Stream with `n = 2`: the usage chunk arrives with one index's `stream_state`, so a count there covers that index only (3 or 9 here, where coupled reports the sum, 12) while `completion_tokens` from generate covers both. The details stay `null` instead of a partial number, with either index's state:

Compares usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens with the sum of the reasoning tokens over both indices. sent with state of index 0: {"prompt_tokens": 10, "total_tokens": 35, "completion_tokens": 25, "prompt_tokens_details": null, "completion_tokens_details": null} usage chunk sent with state of index 1: would report sum=12 completion_tokens from generate (both indexes) = 25 ```
The 3 new tests on the base commit 39e6a1aafc (test files copied over) and on this branch: ```bash pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender.py -k test_e2e_parsed_usage_details pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py -k test_stream_parsed_usage_details ``` Before: ```text > assert usage["completion_tokens_details"]["reasoning_tokens"] == reasoning_tokens E TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable FAILED tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender.py::test_e2e_parsed_usage_details 1 failed, 90 deselected, 14 warnings in 32.91s > assert usage["completion_tokens_details"]["reasoning_tokens"] == reasoning_tokens E TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable > assert usage["prompt_tokens_details"]["cached_tokens"] == 4 E TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable FAILED tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py::test_stream_parsed_usage_details FAILED tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py::test_stream_parsed_usage_details_n_gt_1_no_reasoning_tokens 2 failed, 122 deselected, 14 warnings in 32.80s ``` After: ```text 1 passed, 90 deselected, 14 warnings in 33.98s 2 passed, 122 deselected, 14 warnings in 33.23s ``` Both files in full on this branch: ```bash pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender.py pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py ``` ```text 91 passed, 14 warnings in 227.08s (0:03:47) 123 passed, 1 xfailed, 14 warnings in 151.96s (0:02:31) ``` ## Details `/v1/chat/completions` counts `reasoning_tokens` with the reasoning parser and keeps the generate server's `cached_tokens`; commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Fix MoE LoRA correctness under DP + EP
commits.pr_body:
With data parallelism and expert parallelism, MoE LoRA runs on tokens dispatched from other DP ranks, but three places assumed the experts only see the local batch:

- LoRAKernelMeta.prepare_tensors returned before copying the token->slot mapping for batches without LoRA, so the EP dispatch sent the previous batch's slots to the other ranks.
- add_lora_fused_moe / moe_lora_align_block_size (and the TRTLLM MXFP4 LoRA experts) gated the dispatched batch on this rank's no-LoRA flag and active-slot stats.
- An idle DP rank's dummy batch activated warmup LoRAs and then removed every adapter on that rank.

Consolidates #61714 and #63526, adapted to the Model Runner V1 removal (#63373), and adds a DP=2 + EP end-to-end test.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Accept FastAPI boolean spellings for reset_connector
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

#57810 added a `reset_connector` query parameter to `POST /sleep` and `POST /release_kv_cache_memory`. Python parses it as a FastAPI `bool`, so `reset_connector=False` (what `requests` sends for `params={"reset_connector": False}`) or `0` is accepted; the Rust frontend parsed it as a plain serde `bool` and returned 400. This PR parses it with the existing `deserialize_query_bool`, as the other boolean query parameters on these routes already are (#65372).

## Claims

- `POST /sleep?reset_connector=False` and `POST /release_kv_cache_memory?reset_connector=0` reach the engine with `reset_connector=false` instead of returning 400.
- Invalid values such as `reset_connector=maybe` still return 400 before any engine call, as in Python.

## Validation

Rust CI set (`.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh`) on this branch, based on `000a53c272`:

```bash
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check                    # clean
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                                           # clean
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans # clean
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings  # clean
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2585 tests run: 2585 passed, 13 skipped
```

`sleep_route_forwards_reset_connector_opt_out` and `release_kv_cache_memory_route_forwards_reset_connector_opt_out` now send `reset_connector=False` and `reset_connector=0` and check that `false` reaches the engine utility call; both fail with 400 without the fix. `sleep_route_rejects_invalid_query_before_engine_dispatch` adds `reset_connector=maybe`.

## Details

**Layering.** The parameter is a field of the HTTP route's query DTOs (`SleepParams`, `ReleaseKvCacheMemoryParams` in `routes/sleep.rs`), so the spelling is accepted there with the existing helper. The gRPC `SleepRequest.reset_connector` is a typed `optional bool` and needs nothing; `level` and `mode` already match Python's parsing.

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR changes this parameter in the Rust frontend.

**AI assistance.** This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). The human submitter reviewed every changed line and the validation results.
